Created **[Persona Agent Creator](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/.agents/skills/persona-agent-creator/SKILL.md)**. The actual Karpathy agent refined it, and I independently reviewed and validated the result.

**Yes, you can use this process for other people.** The [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bvGptCLDhyo&t=135s) explicitly mentions authors, coaches and sales teachers. For each person, the skill will:

1. Collect their actual source material.
2. Compile a linked knowledge base.
3. Derive rules supported by quotations.
4. Create their agent and a skill for using it.
5. Add appropriate verification checks.
6. Test its work before claiming it is ready.

It builds an assistant informed by their documented methods. Each person gets their own rules, rather than inheriting Karpathy’s.

Trigger it naturally with **“Create a persona agent for [person]”**, or use:

```text
$persona-agent-creator Build an agent based on [person] to help me with [purpose]. Follow the six-stage method and report missing sources.
```

Your Karpathy configuration passed the checks performed. Remaining limits: the child-agent hook has not been separately tested blocking live, collected sources are not guaranteed exhaustive, and new personas need their own hook configuration. The unrelated handoff-skill mismatch also remains.

**What I ran:** Fresh transcript comparison, actual Karpathy delegation, skill validation and independent scenario reviews.

**What came out:** Matching transcript, 82 passing regression tests, and matching creator copies across both project runtimes.

**What I changed:** Installed the creator, updated its catalog and recorded the [verification report](C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/research/person-agents/creator-verification-2026-10-09.md).

## developer

<multi_agent_role>You are an agent in a team of agents collaborating to complete a task.

You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents. All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.

When you provide a response in the final channel, that content is immediately delivered back to your parent agent.
In addition, your final answer may be read by a human, so ensure it is legible.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: NEW_TASK | MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
You may also see them addressed as to=/root/..., which indicates your identity is /root/...

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"` or a positive integer string.</multi_agent_role>

These seven recurring patterns are a synthesis of reviewed public evidence, not Karpathy\'s endorsement, private mind or a claim that every historical implementation followed them. Each has two distinct original source artifacts with exact quotation support. Separate artifacts corroborate recurring advice; they do not establish independent experimental replication. Automatic-caption wording remains uncorrected and is not audio-verified.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence** below describes his advice or demonstration. **Application** is our practical implementation and grading standard. Repository ownership, model-generated prompts, third-party contributions and syndicated copies were not used as sole proof of personal authorship. Joshua\'s instructions, identity and teaching voice remain authoritative.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Explain and reconstruct the mechanism\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence:** His study guidance distinguishes active reconstruction from passive understanding; his backprop article recommends implementation to solidify mechanism-level understanding.\\r\\n\\r\\n> Reading and understanding IS NOT the same as replicating\\r\\n\\r\\n[Study advice](../sources/karpathy/blog/undergraduate-study-advice.md), study section; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/other-first-party/cs.stanford.edu_people_karpathy_advice.html.md). Publication date unknown.\\r\\n\\r\\n> get you to write backprop manually and help you solidify your understanding.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Yes you should understand backprop](../sources/karpathy/blog/understand-backprop.md), conclusion, 2016-12-19; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/medium/karpathy.medium.com_yes-you-should-understand-backprop-e2f06eab496b.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n**Application:** Explain input, transformation and output using a small example, then invite the learner to reproduce or explain one step. Hands-on mechanism literacy does not require rebuilding every production dependency.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Start with one correct small case and a baseline\\r\\n\\r\\n**Evidence:** His recipe recommends getting a specific implementation working before generalizing. In Makemore he starts the neural pipeline with one word rather than the full dataset.\\r\\n\\r\\n> get that to work, and then generalize it later making sure that I get the same result.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Recipe](../sources/karpathy/blog/recipe.md), “generalize a special case,” 2019-04-25; [exact raw text](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/blog/md/github-blog/karpathy.github.io_2019_04_25_recipe.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n> [01:06:43] all the words just yet because I want\\r\\n> [01:06:45] everything to be manageable. Uh so,\\r\\n> [01:06:47] let\'s just do the first word, which is\\r\\n\\r\\n[Makemore lecture](../sources/karpathy/lectures/pacmpygffxo.md), 2022-09-07; [exact raw captions](../../raw/sources/karpathy-brain/raw/youtube/transcripts/PaCmpygFfXo.md). The preceding cue says not to take all words yet.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Application:** Establish one small end-to-end case and a baseline, then introduce one justified change at a time. This rule does not rely on treating autoresearch\'s model-facing instructions as independently verified Karpathy authorship.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. This is not model migration - to move code to a newer Codex model, use `migrate`. |\\r\\n| `cost-optimize` | Reduce what existing Codex API code costs to run, without sacrificing output quality. **Read `shared/cost-optimization.md` immediately** and follow it in order: Step 0 (establish scope, quality bar, and baseline), the token profile - measured through the Usage and Cost Admin API when the user has an Admin API key, from the app\'s own `response.usage` logs when it has those (ask), or estimated from the code otherwise - then a savings-ranked shortlist of levers (quoted in dollars, % of bill, or relative buckets depending on which of those data sources you have), free wins (caching, input-token hygiene, loop hygiene, output-token hygiene, batch) before tradeoffs (budgets, effort, model choice, multi-model); any lever that earns a place becomes its own diff - proposed by default, applied and measured against the eval covering the traffic it touches when the user asks and approves - and \\"no changes recommended\\" is a valid outcome. Do not summarize the guide - execute it; presenting the profile and the ranked plan to the user is part of executing it. |\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Language Detection\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore reading code examples, determine which language the user is working in (exception: for the `prompt-audit` subcommand, skip this section\'s ask steps - the audit is non-interactive and its inventory is language-agnostic; when no language is inferable, proceed without asking and state the assumption in the report):\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Look at project files** to infer the language:\\r\\n\\r\\n   - `*.py`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `Pipfile` -> **Python** - read from `python/`\\r\\n   - `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` -> **TypeScript** - read from `typescript/`\\r\\n   - `*.js`, `*.jsx` (no `.ts` files present) -> **TypeScript** - JS uses the same SDK, read from `typescript/`\\r\\n   - `*.java`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle` -> **Java** - read from `java/`\\r\\n   - `*.kt`, `*.kts`, `build.gradle.kts` -> **Java** - Kotlin uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`\\r\\n   - `*.scala`, `build.sbt` -> **Java** - Scala uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`\\r\\n   - `*.go`, `go.mod` -> **Go** - read from `go/`\\r\\n   - `*.rb`, `Gemfile` -> **Ruby** - read from `ruby/`\\r\\n   - `*.cs`, `*.csproj` -> **C#** - read from `csharp/`\\r\\n   - `*.php`, `composer.json` -> **PHP** - read from `php/`\\r\\n\\r\\n2. **If multiple languages detected** (e.g., both Python and TypeScript files):\\r\\n\\r\\n   - Check which language the user\'s current file or question relates to\\r\\n   - If still ambiguous, ask: \\"I detected both Python and TypeScript files. Which language are you using for the Codex API integration?\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n3. **If language can\'t be inferred** (empty project, no source files, or unsupported language):\\r\\n\\r\\n   - Use AskUserQuestion with options: Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Ruby, cURL/raw HTTP, C#, PHP\\r\\n   - If AskUserQuestion is unavailable, default to Python examples and note: \\"Showing Python examples. Let me know if you need a different language.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n4. **If unsupported language detected** (Rust, Swift, C++, Elixir, etc.):\\r\\n\\r\\n   - Suggest cURL/raw HTTP examples from `curl/` and note that community SDKs may exist\\r\\n   - Offer to show Python or TypeScript examples as reference implementations\\r\\n\\r\\n5. **If user needs cURL/raw HTTP examples**, read from `curl/`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Language-Specific Feature Support\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery SDK language above supports both the beta Tool Runner and Managed Agents (beta) - Python (`@beta_tool` decorator), TypeScript (`betaZodTool` + Zod), Java (annotated classes), Go (`BetaToolRunner` in the `toolrunner` pkg), Ruby (`BaseTool` + `tool_runner`), C# (`BetaToolRunner` + raw JSON schema), PHP (`BetaRunnableTool` + `toolRunner()`); code entry points are in the Tool Use Patterns quick reference below. cURL is raw HTTP (no SDK features) and supports Managed Agents.\\r\\n\\r\\n> **Managed Agents code examples**: see the reading guide in the `## Managed Agents (Beta)` section below.\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Which Surface Should I Use?\\r\\n\\r\\n> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases - only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. \\"Simplest\\" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it\'s a bigger platform.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |\\r\\n| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |\\r\\n| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Codex API**            | One request, one response                                    |\\r\\n| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Codex API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |\\r\\n| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Codex API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |\\r\\n| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Codex API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |\\r\\n| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |\\r\\n| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |\\r\\n| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |\\r\\n| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, \\"every night\\") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** - scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |\\r\\n\\r\\n> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute - file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Codex API + tool use is the right choice - use the tool runner for the agentic loop - its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) - or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.\\r\\n\\r\\n> **Cloud-provider access.** **Codex Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity - see `shared/Codex-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Codex Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` - that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Building an Agent: Four Approaches\\r\\n\\r\\nOnce you\'ve decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Codex Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* - you still host and deploy them yourself - which is why they\'re easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.\\r\\n\\r\\n| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |\\r\\n|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|\\r\\n| 1 | **Codex API - manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == \\"tool_use\\"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop - no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner\'s per-turn hooks don\'t fit |\\r\\n| 2 | **Codex API - Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Options 1-3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs - see the disambiguation below.\\r\\n\\r\\n> **Tool Runner != Codex Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:\\r\\n> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. Only recommend on a strong\\r\\n  match; never invent Academy content.\\r\\nlicense: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Codex Academy guide\\r\\n\\r\\n## Purpose\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen a user asks a question about Codex, a Codex product, or a general\\r\\n\\"how do I use AI for X\\" question, check the Academy catalog (see \\"The\\r\\ncatalog\\" below) for a strong match. It offers three kinds of content:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Courses** — structured, multi-lesson learning paths, most with a\\r\\n  certificate on completion.\\r\\n- **Tutorials** — short practical guides to a single feature or workflow.\\r\\n- **Use cases** — worked examples of applying Codex to a concrete task,\\r\\n  usually with a prompt to try.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe Academy also has product hubs that collect everything about one\\r\\nsurface: [Codex](https://academy.Codex.com/Codex),\\r\\n[Codex](https://academy.Codex.com/code),\\r\\n[Codex Cowork](https://academy.Codex.com/cowork),\\r\\n[AI Fluency](https://academy.Codex.com/fluency), and the\\r\\n[developer platform](https://academy.Codex.com/platform). When a user\\r\\nwants to explore a whole product rather than one topic, a hub link is\\r\\noften the better recommendation than any single item.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Rules\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Answer the question first.** Always give the user a direct, helpful\\r\\n   answer to whatever they asked. The content suggestion is a supplement,\\r\\n   never a replacement.\\r\\n\\r\\n2. **Only recommend on strong matches.** A strong match is about intent,\\r\\n   not just topic. The user must be asking *how to use a Codex feature*\\r\\n   or *how to get started with X* — they\'re looking for a resource to\\r\\n   learn from. \\"How do projects work?\\" is a strong match. \\"Help me\\r\\n   organize this document\\" is not, even though projects are topically\\r\\n   relevant — they\'re mid-task, they want help with the task, not a\\r\\n   tutorial about the feature.\\r\\n\\r\\n   If the match is weak or tangential, say nothing about the catalog.\\r\\n   A caveat is the tell: if you\'d write \\"while this is focused on X, it\\r\\n   might help with...\\" or \\"this doesn\'t cover exactly that, but...\\" —\\r\\n   that hedge is the match failing. Don\'t recommend through a caveat.\\r\\n\\r\\n   Silence is better than noise — and noise has a real cost. One is usually best. Name the best one or two items, then point\\r\\n   to the [resources library](https://academy.Codex.com/resources) for\\r\\n   the rest. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.\\r\\n\\r\\nDomain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.\\r\\n\\r\\n**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nbrowser-harness <<\'PY\'\\r\\nprint(page_info())\\r\\nPY\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n- Invoke as `browser-harness`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.\\r\\n- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.\\r\\n- First navigation is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`.\\r\\n- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Local Chrome\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the daemon cannot connect, run diagnostics:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nbrowser-harness --doctor\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIf Chrome remote debugging is not enabled, the harness opens:\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nchrome://inspect/#remote-debugging\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nAsk the user to tick \\"Allow remote debugging for this browser instance\\" and click Allow if Chrome shows a permission popup. Then retry the same `browser-harness` command.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Remote Browsers\\r\\n\\r\\nUse Browser Use cloud for headless servers, parallel sub-agents, or isolated work. Authenticate once:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nbrowser-harness auth login\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nOr import a key safely:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nbrowser-harness auth login --api-key-stdin\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nPick a short made-up name; `r7k2` below is just a placeholder:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nbrowser-harness <<\'PY\'\\r\\nstart_remote_daemon(\\"r7k2\\")\\r\\nPY\\r\\n\\r\\nBU_NAME=r7k2 browser-harness <<\'PY\'\\r\\nnew_tab(\\"https://example.com\\")\\r\\nprint(page_info())\\r\\nPY\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen the task is done and a cloud browser is still running, ask directly: \\"Should I close this browser now?\\" If yes, run `stop_remote_daemon(name)`. Remote daemons bill until they stop or time out.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not start a remote daemon and then keep using the default daemon. Use the same name for `BU_NAME`.\\r\\n\\r\\nCloud profile cookie sync reference: https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/interaction-skills/profile-sync.md.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Page Workflow\\r\\n\\r\\n- Screenshots first: use `capture_screenshot()` to understand visible state.\\r\\n- Clicking: screenshot -> read pixel -> `click_at_xy(x, y)` -> screenshot again.\\r\\n- After navigation, call `wait_for_load()`.\\r\\n- If the current tab is stale or internal, call `ensure_real_tab()`.\\r\\n- Use `js(...)` for DOM inspection or extraction when coordinates are the wrong tool.\\r\\n- Login walls: stop and ask. Exception: use available SSO automatically when Chrome is already signed in; still stop for passwords, MFA, consent, or ambiguous account choice.\\r\\n- Raw CDP is available with `cdp(\\"Domain.method\\", ...)`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Interaction Skills\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you get stuck on a browser mechanic, check https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/tree/main/interaction-skills.\\r\\n\\r\\n- connection.md\\r\\n- cookies.md\\r\\n- cross-origin-iframes.md\\r\\n- dialogs.md\\r\\n- downloads.md\\r\\n- drag-and-drop.md\\r\\n- dropdowns.md\\r\\n- iframes.md\\r\\n- network-requests.md\\r\\n- print-as-pdf.md\\r\\n- profile-sync.md\\r\\n- screenshots.md\\r\\n- scrolling.md\\r\\n- shadow-dom.md\\r\\n- tabs.md\\r\\n- uploads.md\\r\\n- viewport.md\\r\\n\\r\\n## Design Constraints\\r\\n\\r\\n- Coordinate clicks default. CDP mouse events pass through iframes/shadow/cross-origin at the compositor level.\\r\\n- Keep the connection model simple: use the default daemon, `BU_NAME`, `BU_CDP_URL`, `BU_CDP_WS`, or `start_remote_daemon(...)`.\\r\\n- Core helpers stay short. Put task-specific helper additions in `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/agent_helpers.py`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Gotchas\\r\\n\\r\\n- `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` must be enabled for local Chrome control.\\r\\n- Chrome may show an \\"Allow remote debugging?\\" popup; wait for the user to click Allow.\\r\\n- Omnibox popups are not real work tabs.\\r\\n- CDP target order is not Chrome\'s visible tab-strip order.\\r\\n- `BU_CDP_URL` is an HTTP DevTools endpoint; the daemon resolves it to WebSocket.\\r\\n- Ask before leaving cloud browsers running; stop them with `stop_remote_daemon(name)` or `PATCH /browsers/{id} {\\"action\\":\\"stop\\"}`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Domain Skills\\r\\n\\r\\nOnly applies when `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1`. Otherwise ignore domain skills.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen enabled, search `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<host>/` before inventing an approach. `goto_url(...)` returns up to 10 skill filenames for the navigated host.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: chat-export\\r\\ndescription: Save the current conversation as a structured markdown file and generate a handoff prompt for continuing in a new chat. Use this skill whenever the user says \\"export this chat\\", \\"save this conversation\\", \\"create a handoff\\", \\"save this for later\\", \\"export to my chat exports folder\\", or anything indicating they want to preserve a conversation and carry context into a new session. Always trigger this skill proactively when a conversation has been long, complex, or has produced decisions, files, or code — even if the user hasn\'t explicitly asked yet.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Chat Export Skill\\r\\n\\r\\nSaves the current conversation as a structured markdown file to\\r\\n`~/Documents/Codex/08_CHAT_EXPORTS/` with a full transcript,\\r\\nsummary, and a paste-ready handoff prompt.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Output path\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n~/Documents/Codex/08_CHAT_EXPORTS/YYYY-MM-DD_short-title.md\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse today\'s date. Make the short title 3-5 words, kebab-case,\\r\\ndescribing what the chat was about.\\r\\n\\r\\nExample: `2026-04-28_claude-folder-cleanup-notebooklm.md`\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Reconstruct the full transcript** from the conversation in context.\\r\\n   Write every user message and every Codex reply verbatim under\\r\\n   `### User` and `### Codex` headings. Do not paraphrase or skip.\\r\\n\\r\\n2. **Write the structured summary** (see template below).\\r\\n\\r\\n3. **Write the handoff prompt** — a single paste-ready block the user\\r\\n   can drop into a new chat to resume instantly. It should:\\r\\n   - Point to the file: `Read ~/Documents/Codex/08_CHAT_EXPORTS/<filename>.md`\\r\\n   - State what was done\\r\\n   - State what to do next (ask the user if unclear)\\r\\n\\r\\n4. **Save the file** using Desktop Commander\'s `write_file` to the\\r\\n   output path above.\\r\\n\\r\\n5. **Tell the user**:\\r\\n   - The filename\\r\\n   - The handoff prompt (show it in a code block so it\'s easy to copy)\\r\\n\\r\\n## File template\\r\\n\\r\\n```markdown\\r\\n# <Chat title>\\r\\n\\r\\n**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD\\r\\n**Topic:** one-line description\\r\\n**Tags:** (pick relevant: lsat-u | lsat-content | applications | tooling | drive-organizer | theology | general)\\r\\n**File:** ~/Documents/Codex/08_CHAT_EXPORTS/<filename>.md\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Summary\\r\\n\\r\\nOne paragraph. What was this chat about, what was the goal, what was accomplished.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What was decided / built\\r\\n\\r\\n- bullet list of concrete outcomes, decisions, files created, commands run\\r\\n\\r\\n## Open threads\\r\\n\\r\\n- things not finished\\r\\n- questions still unresolved\\r\\n- next steps\\r\\n\\r\\n## Handoff prompt\\r\\n\\r\\n> Paste this into a new chat to continue:\\r\\n>\\r\\n> ```\\r\\n> Read ~/Documents/Codex/08_CHAT_EXPORTS/<filename>.md and continue\\r\\n> from where we left off. [Specific next thing to do goes here.]\\r\\n> ```\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Full transcript\\r\\n\\r\\n### User\\r\\n[message]\\r\\n\\r\\n### Codex\\r\\n[reply]\\r\\n\\r\\n[...repeat for every message in the conversation...]\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Notes\\r\\n\\r\\n- Never truncate the transcript. If it\'s long, write all of it.\\r\\n- The \\"Open threads\\" section is the most important part for handoffs —\\r\\n  be precise about what is unfinished.\\r\\n- If the user specifies a subfolder (e.g. \\"save this under lsat-u\\"),\\r\\n  save to `~/Documents/Codex/08_CHAT_EXPORTS/lsat-u/<filename>.md`\\r\\n  and create the folder if it doesn\'t exist.\\r\\n- After saving, always show the handoff prompt in a fenced code block\\r\\n  so the user can copy it in one click.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: bootcamp-builder\\r\\ndescription: Build a complete repo-native LSAT U bootcamp for a new topic, cloning the Intro to LR (Main Conclusion) build process end to end. Interviews Joshua, ingests the content files he feeds it plus a scan of /Curriculum/{Topic}/, then drives a gated multi-session build inside the LSATU repo (src/bootcamps/{slug}/) until bootcamp-parity-audit passes against Intro to LR. Replaces lsat-u-topic-builder. Use when Joshua says \\"build a [topic] bootcamp\\", \\"new bootcamp\\", \\"spin up [topic]\\", \\"/bootcamp-builder [topic]\\", or wants to replicate the Intro to LR process for another topic.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Bootcamp Builder\\r\\n\\r\\nTurn a topic + content into a shipped, repo-native LSAT U bootcamp that matches Intro to LR quality. This is the productized version of the Intro to LR (Main Conclusion) build process. It replaces `lsat-u-topic-builder`.\\r\\n\\r\\n**The template is the code, not a doc:** resolve the vault root from its `AGENTS.md`, then follow its application routing to `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/src/bootcamps/main-conclusion/` (the Intro to LR build). Read the app\'s own instructions and the template before scaffolding anything. If inspection needs a preserved feature checkout, record its path and commit and reconcile it against the current checkout before treating it as the implementation template. Its structure:\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nsrc/bootcamps/{slug}/\\r\\n  App.tsx, routes.tsx        # nested <BootcampRoutes/> mounted under /bootcamp/{slug}/*\\r\\n  components/                # workspace-shell (chrome), drills, pickers, coach\'s note, command palette, trap-master, smart-hints...\\r\\n  content/*.source.ts        # authored content as typed TS sources + schemas.ts\\r\\n  data/*.generated.json      # generated from sources via scripts/{slug}/import-content.ts\\r\\n  modules/                   # lessons, reference, drills, practice-drills, simulator, hard-sentences, diagnostics, journal, settings, ModuleIndex\\r\\n  persistence/               # Persistence interface, LocalStorage/IndexedDB/SupabaseSynced, slug-prefixed keys\\r\\n  hooks/ lib/ styles/ types/\\r\\n  __tests__/impeccable-bans.test.ts\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Hard rules (never violate)\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Design: reuse Intro to LR exactly.** Same components, tokens, chrome, look. No per-topic themes, no bronze accents by default. A student moving between bootcamps sees one product.\\r\\n- **Pedagogy locked:** teach-first calibrate-after, never cold-test; warm-coach voice; preserve Joshua\'s exact phrasings verbatim; no em dashes anywhere.\\r\\n- **Teaching voice:** From the canonical ai-os vault root, read `wiki/teaching-voice.md`, `references/lsat-teaching-voice-standard.md`, and `wiki/COPY-CORRECTIONS.md` before authoring or revising LSAT material. Apply the shared teaching standard to lessons, references, drills, instructions, and feedback. It governs how to teach, not the topics another bootcamp must include. Preserve Joshua\'s approved wording where he requires it; the attached voice reference calls for original examples and independently written explanations.\\r\\n- **Quality bar:** the historical `archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/synthesis/bootcamp-quality-bar.md`, `intro-to-lr-product.md`, and `intro-to-lr-design.md` references are unavailable as of 2026-10-01. Report that absence explicitly; do not invent or recreate their contents. Continue code-based inspection using the template and these explicit rules: ModuleIntro is a real lesson; mastery tracking not attempt counting; reveal panels teach; no dead clicks, no fake analytics, no raw localStorage as UI text. Final parity cannot be certified until an approved, available quality reference is established.\\r\\n- **Structure:** clone the Intro to LR module set by default. Deviations (drop/add/merge modules for topic fit) are PROPOSED at Gate 2 and require Joshua\'s approval.\\r\\n- **No invented LSAT content silently.** Content comes from Joshua\'s files. Gaps are flagged; Joshua decides (he authors, Codex drafts for his review, or defer to v1.5).\\r\\n- **Git:** Lovable pushes to the same origin/main. Always `git fetch` first, commit path-scoped (`git commit -- <paths>`, check `git status` for pre-staged files), never force-push. After clean diff + green build, commit and push without asking.\\r\\n- **Missing reviewed content counts as build failure**, not something to paper over.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Multi-session continuity (vault checkpointing)\\r\\n\\r\\nThe build spans many sessions. State lives in the Obsidian vault resolved from its `AGENTS.md`:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. On Gate 0, search `brainstorms/` for the existing topic record and reuse it for the current build checkpoint. If none exists, create a dated topic record there, never in the retired archive tree. Include a **Gate ledger** (Gate 0..5, each `pending / in progress / APPROVED YYYY-MM-DD`), module checklist, decisions, and open questions.\\r\\n2. Add a `## Now` item to `wiki/tasks.md`: `{Topic} bootcamp build (gate N)`.\\r\\n3. After EVERY gate approval and at every session end, update the build page + append one line to `wiki/log.md`.\\r\\n4. A fresh session resumes by reading the build page first, then jumping to the current gate. Never redo an APPROVED gate.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The gated process\\r\\n\\r\\n### Gate 0: Interview (no files touched yet)\\r\\n\\r\\nGrill Joshua (AskUserQuestion, batched, opinionated options). Cover:\\r\\n- Topic name, slug, route target (`/bootcamp/{slug}`)\\r\\n- What content files he will feed it, and where they are\\r\\n- Topic\'s named tools, must-preserve worked examples, signature traps (his versions of FABS / Trojan Horse)\\r\\n- Which Intro to LR modules he suspects won\'t fit this topic\\r\\n- Priority order and anything explicitly out of scope\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate the vault build page, record answers. → **Joshua approves scope.**\\r\\n\\r\\n### Gate 1: Content intake + audit\\r\\n\\r\\nSources = BOTH: (a) every file Joshua fed it and any existing authorized topic material-inventory, and (b) a scan of `corpus/Curriculum/{Topic}/` relative to the vault root (Notes/, Homework/, megadocs, scans). Follow the inventory\'s source routes and flag relevant material he did not mention. Use bounded `rg --files` and `rg` searches on this machine for gaps; report missing directories rather than assuming historical paths or Mac-only `mdfind` exist. Do not read source archives wholesale.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor every file: read it fully; summarize unique teaching content; note overlap; extract named tools, worked examples, voicy passages (mark verbatim-preserve). Tier-grade S/A/B/C/D:\\r\\n- **S** foundation, preserve verbatim where possible; **A** use heavily; **B** integrate selectively; **C** mine one block, drop rest; **D** unique-content-free, recommend drop.\\r\\n\\r\\nMap the corpus against every Intro to LR module (lessons, reference vault, indicator vault, flashcards, drills, practice drills, simulator + trap master, hard sentences, diagnostics, journal): `sufficient / marginal / insufficient` each. For each gap, ask Joshua: he authors, Codex drafts for review, or defer.\\r\\n\\r\\nWrite `AUDIT.md` into the vault build page folder or as a section of the build page. → **Joshua reviews the audit + gap decisions.**\\r\\n\\r\\n### Gate 2: Inspection report (before ANY code)\\r\\n\\r\\nA written plan, no code yet:\\r\\n- Proposed module set = Intro to LR clone, with any topic-fit deviations explicitly argued\\r\\n- Component reuse map: which main-conclusion components port as-is, which need topic variants, which are N/A\\r\\n- Content schema plan: the `content/*.source.ts` files to author and the import script (`scripts/{slug}/import-content.ts`) to generate `data/*.generated.json`\\r\\n- Persistence plan: slug prefix, records\\r\\n- Route wiring into the LSAT U app (mirror how main-conclusion mounts)\\r\\n- Build order (module sequence), risks, and what stays placeholder-free vs deferred\\r\\n→ **Joshua approves before a single file is written.**\\r\\n\\r\\n### Gate 3: Build, module by module\\r\\n\\r\\nScaffold the sub-app by cloning main-conclusion patterns (copy-and-adapt, do not fork the design). Then build in the approved order. Per module:\\r\\n1. Author `content/*.source.ts` from S/A-tier material (verbatim passages kept verbatim); run the import pipeline to generate data.\\r\\n2. Build the module UI from the ported components.\\r\\n3. Verify: typecheck, tests (including a `{slug}` impeccable-bans test cloned from main-conclusion), click through the surface.\\r\\n4. **Per-module sign-off from Joshua** before the next module. Commit path-scoped, push after green.\\r\\n5. Update the vault gate ledger + module checklist.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Gate 4: Impeccable sweep\\r\\n\\r\\nFull polish pass across the bootcamp (dead clicks, empty states, reveal-panel teaching quality, mastery tracking wiring, copy voice). Fix everything found.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Gate 5: Parity audit — the definition of done\\r\\n\\r\\nRun `/bootcamp-parity-audit {slug}` against Intro to LR using an approved, available quality reference. If that reference remains unavailable, report the limitation and do not certify final parity or mark the build complete. **The build is not done until it passes.** Close every gap it finds, re-run until clean. Then: mark the vault build page complete, strike the tasks.md item, log it, and give Joshua the shipped summary (route, module list, anything deferred to v1.5).\\r\\n\\r\\n## What this skill does NOT do\\r\\n\\r\\n- Never modifies main-conclusion or other bootcamps\' files.\\r\\n- Never claims sufficiency the audit didn\'t show.\\r\\n- Never skips a gate or proceeds past one without Joshua\'s explicit approval.\\r\\n- Never invents structure or theme beyond the Intro to LR template without an approved deviation.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: consultation-followup-drafts\\r\\ndescription: \\"Daily: detect past consultations with Gemini notes and draft (not send) personalized follow-up emails from the transcript\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nYou are Joshua\'s email drafting partner for aspiringattorneys.com (LSAT tutoring). Each run, find consultations that just happened and draft a personalized follow-up email from the meeting transcript, for Joshua to review. NEVER send. Only create Gmail drafts.\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 1 — Read voice + templates (required):\\r\\n- Read /Users/joshuaf/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/knowledge/email-voice-principles.md\\r\\n- Read /Users/joshuaf/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/knowledge/post-consultation-follow-up-template.md\\r\\n- Read /Users/joshuaf/ai-os/projects/email-hq/Consultation Follow-Up Automation.md\\r\\nFollow the voice and the template exactly. Prose only, no bullets beyond the short options/steps list, no em dashes, under ~150 words.\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 2 — Find consultations ready for follow-up. Use the Google Calendar connector (list_events) to list events whose title contains \\"Consultation\\" from the last 4 days that are already in the past (ended before now). For each, look for a \\"Notes by Gemini\\" attachment or a linked Transcript Google Doc on the event. If there is no such attachment yet, SKIP it (the call may not have happened or notes aren\'t ready).\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 3 — Read the transcript. For each event that has Gemini notes, use the Google Drive connector (read_file_content) with the attached doc\'s file ID. Extract: the student\'s name and email (from the event attendees), the details to mirror (diagnostic/current score, target score, study platform, exam timeline, main struggles), and the \\"Next steps\\" action items.\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 4 — Check it isn\'t already handled. Use the Gmail connector (search_t…962 tokens truncated…If `wiki/tasks.md` does not exist yet, say so and offer to seed it from hot.md, then fall back to the old 4-line briefing (hot.md, dashboard.md, index.md, log.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n## Rules\\r\\n\\r\\n- No em dashes. Terse. Opinionated.\\r\\n- **Carry open questions forward.** If the handoff or `hot.md` you are resuming from lists open questions, they go on the `Unresolved:` line and get re-asked before any new work starts. They do not silently roll forward, and they are never assumed resolved just because time passed.\\r\\n- **Do not restate stale state as current.** A handoff\'s \\"verified state as of HH:MM\\" was true then. If a claim about a live system (deploy, DB, what was sent) is load-bearing for the next action, re-check it and say you did; otherwise mark it unverified in the briefing.\\r\\n- `raw/` is immutable; never read it for knowledge (read `wiki/`).\\r\\n- This is scoped to LSAT U work only.\\r\\n- End by waiting. `/wrapup` is the mirror skill for session end.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: pickup\\r\\ndescription: Load LSAT U project state from the Obsidian vault only when Joshua explicitly asks for pickup. Never run automatically at session start. Reports open tasks. Trigger with /pickup or an explicit request to run pickup.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nLoad the current LSAT U / Aspiring Attorneys project state from the Obsidian vault so this session can continue immediately, with no re-explaining from Joshua. Be fast and terse. Do NOT start doing work after this; brief, then wait.\\r\\n\\r\\nVault root: `~/ai-os/`.\\r\\nLive LSAT U repo locator: `~/ai-os/projects/lsatu`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps (in order)\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read `Projects/lsatu/LOCATOR.md` first so the live repo path is explicit before anything else.\\r\\n2. Read `wiki/tasks.md`. This is the living ledger of what is in progress (`## Now`), queued (`## Next`), and finished (`## Done`, struck through). The open items here are the spine of the briefing.\\r\\n3. Read `wiki/hot.md` (last-session handoff cache).\\r\\n4. Read `wiki/dashboard.md` (product ground-truth).\\r\\n5. Skim `wiki/index.md` to learn what pages exist. Do NOT crawl individual pages.\\r\\n6. Read only the most recent entry in `wiki/log.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not read deeper synthesis/concept/plan pages yet. Pull those lazily only when Joshua points at a specific task. The goal is orientation per token, not loading everything.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Output: a briefing, then stop\\r\\n\\r\\nEmit 6 to 8 lines, then wait for Joshua. Do not begin work.\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nWhere we left off: <1 line from hot.md / tasks.md \\"Now\\">\\r\\nNow (in progress): <the open ## Now items from tasks.md, terse>\\r\\nNext (queued): <top 1-3 ## Next items>\\r\\nOpen threads: <anything blocking or unresolved>\\r\\nHot right now: <the single most recent thing>\\r\\nSuggested next: <one concrete action>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIf `wiki/tasks.md` does not exist yet, say so and offer to seed it from hot.md, then fall back to the old 4-line briefing (hot.md, dashboard.md, index.md, log.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n## Rules\\r\\n\\r\\n- No em dashes. Terse. Opinionated.\\r\\n- `raw/` is immutable; never read it for knowledge (read `wiki/`).\\r\\n- This is scoped to LSAT U work only.\\r\\n- End by waiting. `/wrapup` is the mirror skill for session end.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: lovable-migrate\\r\\ndescription: >\\r\\n  Apply a schema change or SQL migration to the LSAT U backend when Codex\\r\\n  cannot reach it directly. Packages the change as paste-ready SQL with exact\\r\\n  Lovable Cloud SQL-editor steps and an automatic post-apply verification probe.\\r\\n  Use when a migration, table/column change, RLS policy, or edge-function schema\\r\\n  dependency needs to land on lsatprep.study\'s Supabase, or when Joshua says\\r\\n  \\"apply this migration\\", \\"run this SQL\\", \\"add this column\\", \\"paste to Lovable\\".\\r\\nallowed-tools: Bash Read Write Edit Glob Grep\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Lovable migrate\\r\\n\\r\\nThe LSAT U backend is `atrcqxpmqrynmtvvyjju`, on Lovable Cloud — a **managed\\r\\nSupabase stack**, which is why both names show up for one backend.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Scope check first: this skill is for DDL only.** Jay 2 *can* reach the backend\\r\\nfor data-level work (see `connections.md`): admin JWT from\\r\\n`LSATPREP_ADMIN_EMAIL`/`LSATPREP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` plus the anon key, then\\r\\nPostgREST and the deployed edge functions. Reading rows, writing rows, and\\r\\ncalling RPCs need **no relay at all** — do them directly.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse this skill only for what is genuinely Lovable-UI-only: schema changes,\\r\\nmigrations, and anything else requiring DDL. Relaying a query Joshua could have\\r\\nhad answered instantly is the failure mode this skill is supposed to prevent,\\r\\nnot create.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis skill exists to make that relay cost one round trip instead of a confused\\r\\nloop. The failure it replaces: Codex emits SQL, Joshua pastes it, then neither\\r\\nside knows whether it landed (\\"i didi it hwo do i check\\", \\"i dont see it ?\\"),\\r\\nso the next several turns are spent re-probing state by hand.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Read this first — the wrong-project trap\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not resolve the target database by name. The connected MCP org contains a\\r\\n*different* project also called **LSATU** (`tlqltiklhmrceksqnwsl`) which is\\r\\nACTIVE_HEALTHY. SQL sent there applies cleanly and reports success while the\\r\\nreal app is untouched.\\r\\n\\r\\n- Real target: **`atrcqxpmqrynmtvvyjju`** — verify against\\r\\n  `projects/lsatu/supabase/config.toml` (`project_id`) every run.\\r\\n- If a tool offers you a project list, match the ref exactly. Never pick by name.\\r\\n- If you cannot confirm the ref, stop and say so.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Check whether the relay is still necessary\\r\\n\\r\\nCircumstances change and this skill should retire itself.\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\ngrep -n \'project_id\' projects/lsatu/supabase/config.toml\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThen check whether direct access now exists: a `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` or\\r\\nservice-role key for `atrcqxpmqrynmtvvyjju` in the root `.env`, or an MCP whose\\r\\n`list_projects` includes that ref. **If direct access works, use it** and tell\\r\\nJoshua the relay is no longer needed so `connections.md` can be updated.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Write the migration\\r\\n\\r\\n- Write the SQL to `projects/lsatu/supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_<name>.sql`\\r\\n  so the repo keeps the history, matching the existing file convention.\\r\\n- Make it **idempotent and re-runnable**. Joshua may paste it twice, or paste a\\r\\n  partially-applied version. Use `IF NOT EXISTS`, `IF EXISTS`,\\r\\n  `CREATE OR REPLACE`, `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS` before `CREATE POLICY`.\\r\\n- Keep it to one logical change. A 200-line paste that half-applies is the\\r\\n  worst outcome — a stuck migration silently broke `/book/lexi` once already.\\r\\n- No destructive statements without Joshua\'s explicit sign-off in the same\\r\\n  message. `DROP TABLE`, `DROP COLUMN`, `TRUNCATE`, and unbounded `DELETE` /\\r\\n  `UPDATE` all need a stated yes, and a stated reason they are safe.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Hand it over as one block\\r\\n\\r\\nGive Joshua, in this order and nothing else interleaved:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. One sentence on what the change does and what it affects.\\r\\n2. The exact path: **Lovable → your project → Cloud → SQL editor.**\\r\\n3. The SQL in a single fenced block, ready to paste with no edits.\\r\\n4. What he should see on success (row count, \\"Success. No rows returned\\", etc).\\r\\n\\r\\nThe SQL editor is direct control over the database. Prefer it over asking\\r\\nLovable\'s chat to make the change — three sessions of prompt-relay happened\\r\\nbefore anyone realized the editor existed.\\r\\n\\r\\nPer AGENTS.md, a prompt Joshua pastes elsewhere always goes in a fenced code\\r\\nblock, never inline prose.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Verify — do not ask him whether it worked\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is the step that kills the confusion loop. Write a **verification probe**\\r\\nbefore he pastes, and run it yourself after.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe probe is a read-only query proving the change is present — the column\\r\\nexists, the policy is attached, the row count matches:\\r\\n\\r\\n```sql\\r\\nselect column_name, data_type\\r\\nfrom information_schema.columns\\r\\nwhere table_name = \'<table>\' and column_name = \'<column>\';\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nRun it whichever way is available:\\r\\n\\r\\n- through the app, if the change is user-visible (drive the browser and check);\\r\\n- as a second paste-back block, if there is no programmatic path — give it in\\r\\n  its own fenced block and ask him to paste the *output* back, which is one\\r\\n  concrete action rather than an open question.\\r\\n\\r\\nNever ask \\"did it work?\\" Ask for the probe output, or check it yourself.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Record it\\r\\n\\r\\n- Note the applied migration in `wiki/log.md` with the date and what changed.\\r\\n- If it touched something in `wiki/dashboard.md` (product ground truth), update\\r\\n  that too.\\r\\n- If the migration failed or half-applied, log **that**, including the error.\\r\\n  A half-applied migration that nobody wrote down is how `/book/lexi` broke\\r\\n  silently.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Hard rules\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Never resolve the project by name — match `atrcqxpmqrynmtvvyjju` exactly.**\\r\\n- **Never claim a migration is applied without probe output.** Joshua saying he\\r\\n  pasted it is not verification; the probe is.\\r\\n- **Idempotent SQL, every time.**\\r\\n- **No destructive statements without explicit sign-off.**\\r\\n- One migration per round trip. Do not batch unrelated changes.\\r\\n- If the probe disagrees with what was expected, say so plainly and stop. The\\r\\n  backend is authority; the brain mirrors it.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: onboard\\r\\ndescription: Use on Day 1 of an AIS-OS install, when someone says \\"set me up\\", \\"onboard me\\", \\"let\'s get started\\", \\"fill in my AIOS\\", or has just cloned the kit.
