If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\nRead a message and extract its body or headers\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws gmail +read --id <ID>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Required | Default | Description |\\r\\n|------|----------|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| `--id` | ✓ | — | The Gmail message ID to read |\\r\\n| `--headers` | — | — | Include headers (From, To, Subject, Date) in the output |\\r\\n| `--format` | — | text | Output format (text, json) |\\r\\n| `--html` | — | — | Return HTML body instead of plain text |\\r\\n| `--dry-run` | — | — | Show the request that would be sent without executing it |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Examples\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws gmail +read --id 18f1a2b3c4d\\r\\ngws gmail +read --id 18f1a2b3c4d --headers\\r\\ngws gmail +read --id 18f1a2b3c4d --format json | jq \'.body\'\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tips\\r\\n\\r\\n- Converts HTML-only messages to plain text automatically.\\r\\n- Handles multipart/alternative and base64 decoding.\\r\\n\\r\\n## See Also\\r\\n\\r\\n- [gws-shared](../gws-shared/SKILL.md) — Global flags and auth\\r\\n- [gws-gmail](../gws-gmail/SKILL.md) — All send, read, and manage email commands\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: google-workspace\\r\\ndescription: \\"Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even \\\\\\"change it\\\\\\" or \\\\\\"add a tab\\\\\\". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Codex\'s own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides\\r\\n\\r\\nThe Google connectors are thin wrappers over Google\'s raw APIs, with almost no guidance of their own. This skill supplies that guidance: which connector does what, the rules that keep edits in the user\'s file, and, in one reference file per app, how each API really behaves. Most of the app-specific rules in the references were tested against Google\'s Docs, Sheets and Slides APIs; the rest were seen through the connectors, and a few have not been checked yet.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Read the reference before you touch the file\\r\\n\\r\\n| Working on | Read first | Why it matters |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| A Google Doc | `references/docs.md` | Docs edits address UTF-16 positions that shift after every insert and go stale after every write. Tabs and pending suggestions change the positions too. |\\r\\n| A Google Sheet | `references/sheets.md` | Both write tools parse input like the Sheets UI, so text can silently become numbers or dates. Formatting needs numeric sheet IDs, 0-based ranges, and field masks without parentheses. |\\r\\n| A Google Slides deck | `references/slides.md` | Positions are in EMU, an element\'s real size is its size times its scale, and an unmasked read can exceed 150 KB for three slides. Slides never shrinks text to fit. |\\r\\n\\r\\nRead the reference for every app the task touches before the first edit. Embedding a Sheets chart in a deck means reading both. The references are short, and skipping one is how edits land in the wrong place.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Check the connectors before you start\\r\\n\\r\\n| Connector | What it can do |\\r\\n|---|---|\\r\\n| Google Drive | Create files, upload and convert content, rename, read a file as text, export (PDF and other formats), search, trash |\\r\\n| Google Docs | Read a doc\'s full structure and edit it in place, directly or as suggestions |\\r\\n| Google Sheets | Read values and structure, write values and formulas, format, add tabs and charts |\\r\\n| Google Slides | Read a deck, add and edit slides, shapes, text, tables, and linked charts |\\r\\n\\r\\nDrive can create all three file types. It can\'t edit a file after that. Without the matching editor connector, every change means a new file and a new link, and the user loses the link they already have.\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Check which Google tools are available in this conversation. On surfaces where tools are deferred, search for and load the tools you need first, such as \\"google sheets update\\". Tool names differ by surface, so use the names your surface lists. If a search returns nothing, list all available tools before deciding the connector is missing, because the tool may exist under a different name.\\r\\n2. If the editor tools are missing, tell the user. When you can list the conversation\'s connectors, say which case it is: a connector that is set up but turned off in this chat (ask them to turn it on in the chat\'s connector settings, then continue), or one that isn\'t connected at all (tell them which connector to add and what it enables).\\r\\n3. With an editor connector missing, a request to create a new file continues with Drive. A change to an existing file stops and asks. See the missing-connector rule in section 2.\\r\\n4. If the user asks only for a new file, create it with Drive. If the editor connector is off, add one line saying edits will need it.\\r\\n\\r\\nExample: \\"I can create the sheet now. If you want changes later, turn on the Google Sheets connector in this chat first. Then I can edit this file, and the link will stay the same.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Rules for every file\\r\\n\\r\\n- **A change goes in the same file.** \\"Change\\", \\"update\\", \\"fix\\", \\"add\\", and \\"switch it to\\" all mean the user wants the same file and link. Do not recreate the file to skip an edit.\\r\\n- **A missing editor connector is a choice for the user, not a workaround for you.** When the user asks for a change to an existing file and the editor connector is missing, your whole reply is a short question, not a deliverable. Building the next-best thing feels helpful, but the user\'s file is still untouched and now there are two artifacts, which is the exact failure this skill exists to prevent. Lead with the fix: name the connector and say that with it on, the edit lands in their existing file and the link stays the same. You may offer an alternative, such as drafted text to paste or a file to import by hand, but only as a named option, and build it only after the user picks it. Example reply, in full: \\"To add the slide to your deck directly, turn on the Google Slides connector in this chat and I\'ll do it. Same deck, same link. Or I can draft the slide as a file you\'d import by hand. Which do you prefer?\\"\\r\\n- **Never trash a file the user didn\'t ask you to delete.** Drive can trash a file, but it can\'t restore one. The Docs, Sheets, and Slides connectors can\'t open a trashed file.\\r\\n- **Read before you edit, and guard the write.** Every Docs and Slides read returns a `revisionId`. Pass it as `writeControl.requiredRevisionId` on the next batch update. If the file changed in between, the whole batch is rejected with a 400 (\\"does not match the latest revision\\") instead of landing on stale positions. Write replies don\'t return the new revision, so read again before the next guarded write. On a rejection, read again and rebuild the requests; never retry without the guard. Sheets is different: the Sheets reads in `references/sheets.md` return no `revisionId`, so read again right before a Sheets write and send it without `writeControl`.\\r\\n- **Put everything for one step in one batch.** Batch requests run in order and atomically: if one is invalid, none apply. One call per logical step is faster and leaves no half-finished state.\\r\\n- **Verify the result.** Read the file again after each edit and check the result before you report it. A tool accepting the call does not mean the content is correct. Each reference has a Verify section.\\r\\n- **Rename with Drive `update_file`.** A rename keeps the same link.\\r\\n- **Link every file you name.** When you name a Google file you created, copied, found, or edited, make its title a link, inside the sentence that says what you did: \\"I added the row to [Team roster](its link).\\" Don\'t set the file apart after a colon or on a line of its own (\\"I\'ve created a file for you: Team roster\\"). If a Drive result says the user can already see or open a file from the chat, leave that file\'s link out unless they ask. Always give the link when the user asks for it, wants to send it to someone, or says they can\'t see or open the file, even if a result said they could. Don\'t tell the user to use a card or preview unless a result said one is shown. After an edit, say that the link stays the same.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Drive, for all three apps\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Find a file:** use Drive search when the user names a file without a link. Confirm the match with the user if more than one file fits.\\r\\n- **Create:** `create_file` with `contentMimeType` set to `application/vnd.google-apps.document`, `.spreadsheet`, or `.presentation` creates an empty file. Uploading content with a source type (HTML, CSV, .xlsx, .pptx) converts it into the matching Google type. Each reference says which route fits that app.\\r\\n- **Read as text:** `read_file_content` returns a compact text rendering: Markdown for a Doc. It is a few KB where the editor connector\'s full read can be over 100 KB, so use it to understand content, then use the editor read when you need positions.\\r\\n- **Export:** `download_file_content` with `exportMimeType: \\"application/pdf\\"` returns the rendered file as base64. It is large (about 65 KB of text for a four-slide deck), so export only for a visual check, and only where you can run code.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Helper scripts\\r\\n\\r\\nThe `scripts/` folder next to this file holds tested helpers. They turn the APIs\' raw JSON into short readable summaries, and turn simple specs into correct request batches, so the error-prone arithmetic never happens by hand. Use them wherever you can run Python. Run them by their full path inside this skill\'s folder; the references write that folder as `<skill>`.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Script | Commands | Used for |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| `docs_index.py` | `outline`, `find`, `new-table`, `fill-table` | Docs positions, text search with bold and suggestion state, adding a filled table in one call, filling an existing table |\\r\\n| `sheets_helper.py` | `range`, `format`, `cells` | A1 ranges to grid ranges, formatting batches from a short spec, reading formulas and error cells |\\r\\n| `slides_helper.py` | `outline`, `build` | Real slide geometry with overflow and overlap warnings, building slides from an inch-based spec |\\r\\n| `render_export.py` | one command | Decoding a PDF export into page images to look at |\\r\\n\\r\\n**Getting JSON to a script.** Large tool results are often saved to a file by the app, and the result tells you the path. Point the script at that path; the scripts read the file as the app saved it. When a result comes back in context and is small (a few KB, such as a masked read or sheet metadata), write it to a file and run the script on it. Don\'t re-type a large result into a file: that doubles the cost and invites copying errors. If a large result was cut off and not saved, read a smaller slice instead (a field mask, a range, or one tab) rather than guessing.\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery script prints `--help` with its full usage. Each reference shows the commands in context.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Common failures across apps\\r\\n\\r\\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| \\"No such tool available\\" | The tool is deferred, or the name is different on this surface | Search for and load the tool. Use the exact name your surface lists. |\\r\\n| Permission denied on a file you created | The file is in the trash | Ask the user to restore it from Drive\'s trash. You can\'t restore it with the connectors. |\\r\\n| 400: required revision ID does not match | The file changed after your read, often because of your own previous write | Read again, rebuild the requests from the new read, and send them with the new revision. |\\r\\n| A whole batch failed on one bad request | Batches are atomic | Fix the named request and resend the full batch. Nothing from the failed call was applied. |\\r\\n| A read is too large or cut off | Unmasked editor reads include everything | Use Drive `read_file_content`, a field mask, a range, or a single tab. Run the helper on a saved result. |\\r\\n| Two files where the user expected one | An edit was done by creating a new file | Make changes in place with the editor connector. Tell the user about the extra file; don\'t trash it without asking. |\\r\\n\\r\\nEach reference ends with the failures specific to that app.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. What the connectors can\'t do\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen a request runs into one of these, say so plainly and do the alternative. *Reported*: seen through the connectors or in their tool schemas. *Untested*: not yet checked.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Codex can\'t see the user\'s screen.** No connector shows what the user has selected, or which file, tab or slide they have open. If \\"this\\" or \\"here\\" isn\'t clear from the chat, ask which file, heading, slide number or cell range they mean. *Reported.*\\r\\n- **Comments:** `read_doc` has returned no comments even with `commentsIncluded: true`. To read comments, use Drive `read_file_content` with `includeComments: true`, or ask the user to paste them. `update_doc` has accepted `insertComment` in one report, although its description is cut before listing it; if that request fails, say you can\'t add comments and offer to list your notes in the reply. *Reported.*\\r\\n- **Suggestion mode can be refused** with \\"Unsupported WriteControl mode\\". Never make direct edits in its place: offer to list the proposed changes or to edit directly (see `references/docs.md`). *Reported.*\\r\\n- **Request lists are cut short.** The `update_doc`, `update_spreadsheet` and `update_presentation` descriptions stop partway through their request lists. Requests missing from the description, such as `addDocumentTab` and `addChart`, have still worked, so try one before deciding it isn\'t supported. *Reported.*\\r\\n- **Uploads travel inside the call.** `create_file` takes the whole file as text or base64, so an .xlsx or .pptx upload is slow and often fails. Build in the file with the editor connectors where you can, and keep uploads small. *Reported.*\\r\\n- **Images need a public URL.** Slides `createImage` and Docs `insertInlineImage` fetch the image from a URL Google can reach; a file from the chat can\'t be inserted this way. For a deck, offer the .pptx route; otherwise ask the user to insert the image. *Untested.*\\r\\n- **A Slides chart must already exist in a Sheet.** Create it there with `addChart`, then embed it with `createSheetsChart`. *Reported.*\\r\\n- **Drive search uses `title`, not `name`.** `name contains \'…\'` fails with \\"Unsupported query field: name\\"; write `title contains \'…\'`, and put the file type in a `mimeType` clause. *Reported.*\\r\\n- **Slides edits may not show in an open deck right away.** If the user doesn\'t see a change, ask them to reload the deck before you change anything again. *Reported; may be fixed.*\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: skill-creator\\r\\ndescription: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources.\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  short-description: Create or update a skill\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Skill Creator\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate skills that give Codex useful, non-obvious guidance without constraining unrelated work.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Core Principles\\r\\n\\r\\n**Assume Codex is already capable.** Include only information that changes its decisions or improves its work. Remove generic advice, repeated instructions, speculative edge cases, and examples that do not materially clarify the task.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Preserve user intent and scope.** A skill should support the requested task, not replace the user\'s chosen product, expand the assignment, modify unrelated configuration, or imply permission for additional external actions. Do not turn a particular example, past failure, or personal preference into a universal requirement.\\r\\n\\r\\nApproval to complete a task does not expand its scope or execution permissions. For retrying or externally mutating workflows, define a stopping condition proportional to the risk.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Match specificity to the risk.** Give the model room to choose an appropriate approach when multiple approaches are reasonable. Use detailed steps, deterministic scripts, or absolute language only when correctness, safety, permissions, or a genuinely fragile workflow requires them.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor open-ended work, describe the outcome and relevant decision criteria. For workflows with a preferred shape, offer useful examples or configurable scripts. Reserve fixed sequences and narrow parameters for operations where deviation would cause a concrete problem. Preserve non-obvious operational invariants, distinguish actual requirements from optional recommendations or local conventions, and avoid restating policies already enforced elsewhere.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Keep discovery cheap and precise.** Skill names and descriptions are available before a skill is loaded. Describe the actual capability and when it applies, adding exclusions only when they prevent likely misrouting. Avoid exhaustive capability lists and catchalls that attract unrelated requests.\\r\\n\\r\\nKeep skills self-contained; refer to another skill or tool only when the requested workflow genuinely requires it and it is available in the target environment. Specialized review, hardening, or audit workflows should apply when requested or genuinely needed, not merely because ordinary work touches the same subject.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Disclose detail progressively.** Keep shared purpose, essential constraints, and useful routing in `SKILL.md`. Put substantial mode-specific guidance, schemas, examples, or procedures in supporting references and read only the references relevant to the current task. A simple self-contained skill does not need a router or extra files.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Anatomy of a Skill\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery skill is a folder containing a required `SKILL.md` file and any optional resources its actual workflow needs:\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nskill-name/\\r\\n|-- SKILL.md                 Required skill instructions\\r\\n|   |-- YAML frontmatter     Required name and description\\r\\n|   `-- Markdown body        Instructions loaded when the skill is used\\r\\n|-- agents/                  Optional UI metadata and invocation policy\\r\\n|   `-- openai.yaml\\r\\n|-- scripts/                 Optional executable helpers\\r\\n|-- references/              Optional documentation loaded as needed\\r\\n`-- assets/                  Optional files used in generated output\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nChoose the structure that fits the actual task. Some skills are short and self-contained; others route among operating modes or delegate complex mechanics to scripts. Avoid creating directories, placeholders, examples, or ancillary documentation without a clear use.\\r\\n\\r\\n### SKILL.md\\r\\n\\r\\nThe YAML frontmatter identifies the skill and determines when it should be considered. Include the required `name` and `description`, and preserve supported optional fields such as existing `metadata` when appropriate.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe Markdown body is loaded only when the skill is used. Put the purpose, essential workflow, real constraints, and useful links there. Keep detailed procedures and examples in supporting references when they are relevant only to particular modes.\\r\\n\\r\\nSkill information is disclosed in three stages:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Name and description:** Available during skill selection, so keep them concise and discriminating.\\r\\n2. **SKILL.md body:** Loaded when the skill applies, so keep its instructions relevant to that task.\\r\\n3. **Supporting resources:** Read or execute only when the current task actually needs them.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe entrypoint should be as short as the task permits while retaining important constraints. A large upper bound is not a target: move conditional detail into references when doing so improves clarity or context use, rather than waiting for the file to become unwieldy.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Scripts\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `scripts/` for executable code when the same logic would otherwise be rewritten repeatedly or deterministic execution materially improves reliability.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Example:** `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` for a PDF operation that would otherwise require recreating the same code.\\r\\n- **Useful for:** Repeated transformations, reliable API operations, data processing, and other concrete automation.\\r\\n- **Validation:** Run new or changed scripts to verify their behavior. Scripts can usually be executed without loading their full implementation into context, although an agent may need to inspect them when patching or adapting them.\\r\\n\\r\\n### References\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `references/` for documentation that is needed only in particular contexts.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Examples:** `references/schema.md` for database tables, `references/policies.md` for domain rules, `references/api_docs.md` for an API, or separate writing guides for different deliverables.\\r\\n- **Useful for:** Schemas, API documentation, company policies, format-specific procedures, detailed workflows, and substantial examples.\\r\\n- **Routing:** Link each reference from `SKILL.md` or another relevant resource and explain when it should be read. Keep information in one place instead of duplicating it across the entrypoint and references.\\r\\n\\r\\nKeep references focused on maintained, task-specific information that changes the agent\'s decisions. Avoid copied manuals, exhaustive catalogs, and generic tutorials already available from authoritative sources. Before removing existing resources, inspect their callers and purpose.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor large references, include useful search terms or a short contents section when that makes the needed material easier to find.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Assets\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `assets/` for files that belong in generated output rather than in the model\'s instructions.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Examples:** `assets/logo.png`, `assets/slides.pptx`, `assets/font.ttf`, or `assets/frontend-template/`.\\r\\n- **Useful for:** Templates, images, fonts, icons, boilerplate projects, and other files copied or adapted into the result.\\r\\n- **Context:** Do not load assets as instructions unless the task requires inspecting them.\\r\\n\\r\\n### UI Metadata and Invocation Policy\\r\\n\\r\\n`agents/openai.yaml` can provide UI-facing metadata such as `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt`, along with invocation policy. When creating or updating those settings, read [references/openai_yaml.md](references/openai_yaml.md) and keep the values consistent with the skill.\\r\\n\\r\\nAutomatic skill selection is allowed by default. Change that default only when the user explicitly requests an explicit-only skill:\\r\\n\\r\\n```yaml\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n  allow_implicit_invocation: false\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThis keeps the skill available when explicitly invoked as `$skill-name` without adding it to the model context automatically. Preserve unrelated existing UI, policy, and dependency fields when updating `agents/openai.yaml`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe initializer creates this file automatically. For new or interface-only metadata, generate it with:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nscripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe generator replaces the entire file. If an existing file contains `policy` or `dependencies`, update only the intended fields in place instead of regenerating it.\\r\\n\\r\\nInclude optional interface fields only when the user provides or requests them.\\r\\n\\r\\n### What Not to Include\\r\\n\\r\\nInclude files that directly support the skill\'s work. Avoid adding a `README.md`, installation guide, changelog, duplicated quick reference, or other auxiliary documentation unless a specific task or packaging requirement calls for it.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Progressive Disclosure in Practice\\r\\n\\r\\nFor a skill with multiple substantial modes, keep the shared guidance and mode-selection criteria in `SKILL.md`. Link each supporting reference where its use becomes relevant. Do not load every reference by default, duplicate reference content in the entrypoint, or add a routing layer when there is nothing meaningful to route.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor example, a deployment skill can keep provider selection in `SKILL.md` and separate provider details:\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\ncloud-deploy/\\r\\n|-- SKILL.md\\r\\n`-- references/\\r\\n    |-- aws.md\\r\\n    |-- gcp.md\\r\\n    `-- azure.md\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen the user chooses AWS, read `references/aws.md`; do not also load the GCP and Azure guides. The same pattern can separate business domains, deliverable types, or other genuinely distinct operating modes.\\r\\n\\r\\nA short skill can instead route to details only when an advanced operation needs them:\\r\\n\\r\\n```markdown\\r\\n## Documents\\r\\n\\r\\nHandle ordinary edits directly.\\r\\n\\r\\n- For tracked changes, read [references/redlining.md](references/redlining.md).\\r\\n- For document internals, read [references/ooxml.md](references/ooxml.md).\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThese examples illustrate options, not a required structure. Choose the organization that makes the skill easier to use without loading irrelevant material.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Create or Update a Skill\\r\\n\\r\\nAdapt the work to the request. Creating a complex new skill may involve understanding realistic use cases, choosing supporting resources, initializing files, writing instructions, and validating the result. A narrow update to an existing skill may require only a focused edit and validation.\\r\\n\\r\\nAsk clarifying questions only when the missing information matters and cannot be reasonably inferred. Respect a user-specified location; otherwise create discoverable skills in `$CODEX_HOME/skills`, or `~/.codex/skills` when `CODEX_HOME` is unset.\\r\\n\\r\\nKeep automatic skill selection enabled unless the user explicitly requests an explicit-only skill. When the intended invocation mode is genuinely unclear and matters to the requested workflow, ask whether the user wants normal automatic discovery or explicit-only invocation; otherwise preserve the default. Do not infer explicit-only invocation from sensitive operations or required approvals: keep the skill discoverable and require authorization immediately before the actual mutation. Preserve an existing skill\'s invocation policy unless the user asks to change it.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor a new or substantially revised skill, consider the actual requests it should handle and which reusable resources would improve those tasks:\\r\\n\\r\\n- A repeated PDF transformation may justify a `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` helper.\\r\\n- An application-building workflow may benefit from an `assets/frontend-template/` starter.\\r\\n- A data-analysis skill may need a `references/schema.md` guide to avoid rediscovering table relationships.\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate those resources only when their concrete benefit justifies them. If the user has already explained the task clearly, proceed without requesting additional examples.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Naming\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.\\r\\n- Keep names under 64 characters and prefer short action-oriented names.\\r\\n- Namespace by tool or domain when doing so improves discovery.\\r\\n- Name the skill folder after the skill.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Initialize a New Skill\\r\\n\\r\\nFor a new skill, use the bundled initializer when it helps create the required files consistently:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nscripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nFor example:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nscripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \\"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\\"\\r\\nscripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \\"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\\" --resources references\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nRequest only the resource directories the skill needs. Use `--examples` only when concrete placeholders would help, and replace or remove them before finishing. Do not initialize an existing skill again.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe initializer creates the skill directory, a concise `SKILL.md` starter, and `agents/openai.yaml`. It creates resource directories and example files only when requested. Pass generated UI values as `--interface key=value` when needed.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Write the Instructions\\r\\n\\r\\nThe frontmatter `description` should briefly explain what the skill does and when it applies. Include a meaningful boundary when similar requests should not activate the skill.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor example:\\r\\n\\r\\n```yaml\\r\\ndescription: Create or edit Word documents when formatting, tracked changes, or comments require document-specific handling.\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nPut detailed workflows, tool choices, examples, and operating modes in the body or relevant references rather than listing them all in the description. Preserve supported optional frontmatter, such as existing `metadata`, when appropriate.\\r\\n\\r\\nWrite only the instructions needed for another Codex instance to perform the task well. State the desired outcome, non-obvious context, real constraints, and relevant references or tools. Preserve the user\'s explicit choices and existing authorization boundaries. Avoid prescribing a fixed structure, process, or number of steps when the task does not require one.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Validate and Iterate\\r\\n\\r\\nValidate the completed skill with:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nscripts/quick_validate.py <path/to/skill-folder>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe validator checks frontmatter, naming, and unfinished scaffold placeholders; it does not prove that the skill makes good decisions. Also check that descriptions remain discriminating, instructions preserve user intent, references are discoverable, and any added scripts actually work.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen testing is warranted, verify observable behavior or meaningful invariants. Avoid tests that merely match generated wording, headings, or regex patterns.\\r\\n\\r\\nImprove the skill based on real usage or demonstrated failures. Prefer a narrow correction to accumulating universal rules for every observed example.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Independent Forward-Testing\\r\\n\\r\\nUse an independent subagent pass when a skill is sufficiently complex or risky that realistic behavioral validation would add meaningful confidence, and when delegation is available and authorized. Ordinary creation or small edits do not automatically require subagents.\\r\\n\\r\\nGive the evaluating agent a realistic user request, the skill, and the minimum raw artifacts needed to perform the task. Do not provide the intended answer, suspected bug, proposed fix, or prior conclusions unless the evaluation genuinely requires them.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor example:\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nUse $skill-name at /path/to/skill-name to complete this realistic request.\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nKeep the evaluation scoped to permitted resources and side effects. Use an isolated temporary workspace for generated artifacts so they do not enter the working tree or contaminate later evaluations. Ask for approval when the proposed evaluation would require additional authorization, affect a live production system, or impose substantial time or cost. Review the actual outcome and artifacts, then make only changes supported by the observed behavior.\\r\\n"}'}]

Preserve its spherical composition, colored categories, central orb, restrained connection particles, Cinema mode, and interactive growth replay.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe command is `/3d-brain` in Codex. Work in the current assistant; no subagents, external services, API keys, paid assets, or deployment are required.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Find the AIOS and the package\\r\\n\\r\\nRead the applicable local operating manual and relevant index. Establish the actual AIOS root; do not scan an unrelated ancestor or all of the user\'s home directory. Resolve this skill\'s own directory from the loaded `SKILL.md`; all package paths below are relative to it, regardless of whether it lives in `.Codex/skills`, `.agents/skills`, or a plugin.\\r\\n\\r\\nRead [the portable spec](references/portable-spec.md) and [the config guide](references/config.md). Check Node.js 22 or newer. Use the user\'s existing Node runtime. If unavailable, explain that Node is required and follow the host\'s installation/approval policy.\\r\\n\\r\\nRun the path-only discovery helper:\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nnode <skill-directory>/scripts/discover.mjs --root <AIOS-root>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIt lists candidate folders, not their contents. Never promise virality.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: booking-link\\r\\ndescription: Use whenever Joshua wants a one-off booking link for LSAT U — \\"make me a link for Dakota at 7:15 tomorrow\\", \\"send her a link to book tonight\\", \\"one-off link, $60\\", \\"short notice link\\", \\"I need a link she can schedule herself with\\". Mints a single-use URL that sells exactly one session at a price you set, optionally pinned to one exact time, and closes after she books. Also covers listing and revoking existing links.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# One-off booking links\\r\\n\\r\\nA URL Joshua sends to one person. She opens it, books one session, pays, and\\r\\ngets the Google Meet invite from the ordinary booking flow. Then the link\\r\\ncloses.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Authorization\\r\\n\\r\\nMinting a link is pre-authorized. Joshua asking for a link means make it now —\\r\\ndo not ask permission, ask only for the facts you actually need.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Never send the link anywhere.** Print it and hand it to Joshua. He decides who\\r\\ngets it. A link is a Bearer [REDACTED]: whoever holds it can book that slot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What you need before running\\r\\n\\r\\nOnly two things are required, and one has a default:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Price** in dollars. Required — links always charge, and the standard rate is\\r\\n  $45 but a given person may pay something else. Ask for nothing you were not given.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Running it\\r\\n\\r\\nFrom `~/ai-os/projects/lsatu`:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nnpm run booking:link -- --for \\"Dakota\\" --price 45 --at \\"2026-09-10 19:15\\"\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nTimes in `--at` are wall-clock in Joshua\'s booking timezone (`America/Toronto`),\\r\\nformat `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm`, 24-hour. Convert \\"7:15pm tomorrow\\" yourself — resolve\\r\\nrelative dates against today before running, and never pass a relative word\\r\\nthrough.\\r\\n\\r\\nIt prints the URL, the price, the time, and how many times the link can sell.\\r\\nGive Joshua the URL exactly as printed.\\r\\n\\r\\n### The flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Default | What it does |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| `--for` | — | Who the link is for. Note only, never in the URL. |\\r\\n| `--price` | — | Dollars. Required. |\\r\\n| `--at` | none | Pin one exact time. See below. |\\r\\n| `--minutes` | 70 | Session length. |\\r\\n| `--notice` | 1440, or 0 with `--at` | Minimum notice in minutes. `0` means \\"bookable right now\\". |\\r\\n| `--window` | 6 | How many business days ahead the picker reaches. |\\r\\n| `--label` | \\"LSAT Session\\" | The title she sees on the page. |\\r\\n| `--note` | auto | Admin reminder of who and why. |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Pinned versus picker\\r\\n\\r\\n**`--at` pins one time.** She sees only that time and confirms it. This is the right shape for \\"I have a gap\\r\\nat 7:15 tonight, let her take it.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n**Without `--at` she gets a calendar** of open times, still inside the weekly\\r\\nhours. Use `--notice 0` for a short-notice link she can book today, and\\r\\n`--window` to control how far ahead it reaches.\\r\\n\\r\\nDouble-booking is never skipped either way. A pinned time that clashes with\\r\\nsomething already on the calendar is refused at mint time — the script deletes\\r\\nthe link and tells you what it hit — and refused again inside the booking\\r\\ntransaction.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Listing and revoking\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nnpm run booking:link -- --list\\r\\nnpm run booking:link -- --revoke <slug>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n`--list` shows every one-off link with its state: `open`, `used`, or `revoked`.\\r\\nRevoking is immediate and the URL stops resolving.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Reading the outcome honestly\\r\\n\\r\\n- **\\"clashes with something already on your calendar\\"** — the time is taken. No\\r\\n  link was created. Tell Joshua what he asked for is not free and offer to pick\\r\\n  another time; do not silently mint a different one.\\r\\n- **\\"would have no open times at all\\"** — a picker link whose window and weekly\\r\\n  hours produce nothing. Usually `--window` is too small or the hours are empty.\\r\\n- **A time in the past** is refused. If Joshua asks for a time that has already\\r\\n  gone by today, say so rather than rolling it to tomorrow on your own.\\r\\n\\r\\n## How it works, so you can debug it\\r\\n\\r\\nA one-off link is a row in `booking_event_types` with a random 10-character slug\\r\\nand `single_use` set. That is the same table defining the ordinary session and\\r\\nthe consultation, and every layer beneath — the page, the `single-session` edge\\r\\nfunction, the SQL slot policy, the claim transaction — is already keyed by event\\r\\nslug. So the link books through exactly the code a normal session books through.\\r\\nThere is no second booking path to keep in sync.\\r\\n\\r\\nSingle use is enforced by the `enforce_booking_event_shape` trigger under a\\r\\nper-slug advisory lock, so two people opening the same link at the same moment\\r\\ncannot both get through. A hold holds the link; letting the checkout expire\\r\\nreleases it; a cancelled or refunded booking stays spent, and a replacement\\r\\nneeds a fresh link.\\r\\n\\r\\nRelevant files:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `scripts/booking-link.ts` — the CLI\\r\\n- `src/pages/OneOffBooking.tsx` and the `/book/x/:slug` route in `src/App.tsx`\\r\\n- `supabase/migrations/20260908120000_one_off_booking_links.sql`\\r\\n- `supabase/functions/single-session/index.ts`\\r\\n\\r\\n## Credentials\\r\\n\\r\\n`LSATPREP_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `LSATPREP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `~/ai-os/.env`, which is\\r\\ngit-ignored. This repo\'s `.env` is tracked in git — never put a credential\\r\\nthere.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: bootcamp-parity-audit\\r\\ndescription: Audit a given LSAT U bootcamp\'s feature and visual parity against the flagship Intro to LR (Main Conclusion) bootcamp, anchored to the quality bar doc. If not given, ask which one, once, don\'t guess.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Anchor documents (read these first, in order)\\r\\n\\r\\n1. `~/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/synthesis/bootcamp-quality-bar.md` — the shared bar every bootcamp finishes to.\\r\\n2. `~/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/synthesis/intro-to-lr-product.md` — the flagship\'s product spec (what \\"done\\" looks like).\\r\\n3. `~/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/synthesis/intro-to-lr-design.md` — the flagship\'s design system (colors, type, role tokens).\\r\\n4. `~/ai-os/wiki/entities/intro-to-lr-bootcamp.md` if it exists, for entity-level facts.\\r\\n5. Use when the user wants to stress-test a plan, get grilled on a design, run a brainstorm or discovery session, extract what\'s in their head into a doc, build up their AI OS context over time, or says \\"grill me\\".\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Grill Me\\r\\n\\r\\nTwo layers. The **interview method** comes from the `grilling` skill and is not restated here. The **capture discipline** below is what this wrapper adds: every answer lands in a durable markdown file, so nothing is lost as context fills up.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Step 1: set up the capture file (BEFORE the first question)\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read the applicable `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, then only the context pages and prior captures relevant to the topic. Starter-kit context lives in `context/`; in an established project follow its declared routes instead of creating a duplicate knowledge store. Reuse facts already supplied; ask about gaps, changes, decisions, and tradeoffs. Installing the skill does not start an interview.\\r\\n2. Create the capture file at `brainstorms/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{topic-slug}.md` (create `brainstorms/` if missing). Every capture lives here, one predictable home regardless of topic. Do NOT scatter captures into project folders. A polished deliverable (plan, map, spec) may later move into the relevant `projects/` folder; the raw capture always stays in `brainstorms/`.\\r\\n   - Get today\'s real date from the clock or shell (`Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd` in PowerShell, `date +%F` in Bash).\\r\\n   - Never overwrite an existing capture. Same date and topic: add a time or unique suffix and create exclusively. Resume an existing capture only when the user asks or clearly refers to that session; read it first and continue its question numbering.\\r\\n   - No topic supplied or inferable: create an `untitled-discovery` capture with goal pending, ask what to explore, record the chosen topic and goal in that same file.\\r\\n3. Write the header immediately: title, date, goal of the session, empty \\"Open flags\\" section.\\r\\n4. Tell the user where you are saving, in one line.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Step 2: run the interview\\r\\n\\r\\nCall the Skill tool with \\"grilling\\". Follow it exactly: map the design tree, ask the whole frontier as a numbered round with a recommended answer per question, dispatch sub-agents for facts instead of asking the user, wait for answers, recompute the frontier, repeat until it is empty.\\r\\n\\r\\nTwo adjustments the capture layer imposes on the method:\\r\\n\\r\\n- For **decisions**, give a recommended answer grounded in context and label it as a recommendation. For **personal or business facts**, ask neutrally. Never lead with invented facts, and never save your inference as the user\'s answer.\\r\\n- When the user **cannot answer** something, capture it as a flag with the right owner and move on. Do not stall the round on it.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Step 3: the checkpoint rule (non-negotiable)\\r\\n\\r\\nAfter EVERY round of answers, BEFORE you ask the next round:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Append one structured entry per answered question: the question, the key facts and decisions from the answer (in the user\'s words where wording matters), and any flags (things they could not answer, plus who should).\\r\\n- Update the running summary when a later answer changes it. Preserve the original entry, mark it superseded, and link to the correcting answer so the reasoning stays traceable.\\r\\n- Read back the saved entries before continuing. If the write fails, say so, keep the answers visible in chat, and do not claim they were saved or collect more answers without a working checkpoint.\\r\\n- Only then ask the next round.\\r\\n\\r\\nNever let two rounds pile up in your head before writing. The file, not your context, is the source of truth. Never make the user ask you to save progress.\\r\\n\\r\\nKeep user-confirmed facts, tentative ideas, your recommendations, and unresolved questions distinguishable in the capture.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Capture file structure\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n# {Topic}: Brainstorm / Discovery Notes\\r\\nDate: {date} · Goal: {one line}\\r\\nStatus: in progress / paused / complete\\r\\nContext sources: {relevant existing pages, if any}\\r\\n\\r\\n## Summary / key decisions\\r\\n(running synthesis, updated as you go)\\r\\n\\r\\n## Q&A log\\r\\n### Round 1\\r\\n#### Q1 - {topic}\\r\\n- Asked: {question}\\r\\n- Recommended: {your recommendation, labeled}\\r\\n- Captured: {user-confirmed facts and decisions, in their words where it matters}\\r\\n- Tentative: {unconfirmed ideas, clearly labeled}\\r\\n- Flags: {open item -> owner}\\r\\n#### Q2 - ...\\r\\n### Round 2\\r\\n...\\r\\n\\r\\n## Open flags (pending input)\\r\\n- {item} -> {who can answer}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## At the end or on pause\\r\\n\\r\\nRespect an explicit stop immediately; do not add a new question. Near the end, offer a completeness backstop (\\"anything we haven\'t touched?\\"). Then:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Read the capture for contradictions or gaps. Mark unresolved conflicts explicitly; do not choose a business fact on the user\'s behalf. Update status and resume point.\\r\\n- For sessions explicitly about building or updating AI OS context, merge user-confirmed durable facts and preferences into the appropriate existing context page, with a dated link back to the capture. Preserve unrelated content. Record confirmed meaningful decisions in the existing decision log without duplicating entries. Unknowns, brainstorm ideas, and your recommendations stay labeled in the capture until confirmed.\\r\\n- For a plan or design interview without a request to update canonical context, the raw capture is the output. Suggest `/link` for routing a useful result, or `/level-up` for turning a selected opportunity into one improvement. Do not run either automatically.\\r\\n- Ensure the operating manual or an existing index routes to `brainstorms/` when capture routing is absent, using the project\'s conventions and preserving shared manual parity. Individual captures do not each need a root-manual entry. Raw captures are dated interview evidence, not automatically current business truth.\\r\\n- Give a short recap: clickable capture path, context pages actually updated, remaining flags, next step or resume point.\\r\\n\\r\\nAs `grilling` requires: do not act on the plan until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Boundaries and verification\\r\\n\\r\\n- Scope is the local interview capture and any requested context updates. No global-memory edits, publication, messages, or external-system changes. Do not request or save credentials; use references or redactions for secrets.\\r\\n- The starter kit ignores `brainstorms/` in Git by default. This does not remove captures already tracked in an existing repository.\\r\\n- Validate a fresh session, a same-day name collision, a resume, a correcting answer, a stop request, and a failed write. Verify that only confirmed facts reach canonical context and that earlier answers remain traceable.\\r\\n"}'}]

Copy the template: `gws drive files copy --params \'{\\"fileId\\": \\"TEMPLATE_DOC_ID\\"}\' --json \'{\\"name\\": \\"Project Brief - Q2 Launch\\"}\'`\\r\\n2. Get the new doc ID from the response\\r\\n3. Add content: `gws docs +write --document-id NEW_DOC_ID --text \'## Project: Q2 Launch\\r\\n\\r\\n### Objective\\r\\nLaunch the new feature by end of Q2.\'`\\r\\n4. Share with team: `gws drive permissions create --params \'{\\"fileId\\": \\"NEW_DOC_ID\\"}\' --json \'{\\"role\\": \\"writer\\", \\"type\\": \\"user\\", \\"emailAddress\\": \\"team@company.com\\"}\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-create-events-from-sheet\\r\\ndescription: \\"Read event data from a Google Sheets spreadsheet and create Google Calendar entries for each row.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-sheets\\r\\n        - gws-calendar\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Create Google Calendar Events from a Sheet\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-sheets`, `gws-calendar`\\r\\n\\r\\nRead event data from a Google Sheets spreadsheet and create Google Calendar entries for each row.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read event data: `gws sheets +read --spreadsheet SHEET_ID --range \\"Events!A2:D\\"`\\r\\n2. For each row, create a calendar event: `gws calendar +insert --summary \'Team Standup\' --start \'2026-01-20T09:00:00\' --end \'2026-01-20T09:30:00\' --attendee alice@company.com --attendee bob@company.com`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-create-expense-tracker\\r\\ndescription: \\"Set up a Google Sheets spreadsheet for tracking expenses with headers and initial entries.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-sheets\\r\\n        - gws-drive\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Create a Google Sheets Expense Tracker\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-sheets`, `gws-drive`\\r\\n\\r\\nSet up a Google Sheets spreadsheet for tracking expenses with headers and initial entries.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Create spreadsheet: `gws drive files create --json \'{\\"name\\": \\"Expense Tracker 2025\\", \\"mimeType\\": \\"application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet\\"}\'`\\r\\n2. Add headers: `gws sheets +append --spreadsheet SHEET_ID --range \'Sheet1\' --values \'[\\"Date\\", \\"Category\\", \\"Description\\", \\"Amount\\"]\'`\\r\\n3. Add first entry: `gws sheets +append --spreadsheet SHEET_ID --range \'Sheet1\' --values \'[\\"2025-01-15\\", \\"Travel\\", \\"Flight to NYC\\", \\"450.00\\"]\'`\\r\\n4. Share with manager: `gws drive permissions create --params \'{\\"fileId\\": \\"SHEET_ID\\"}\' --json \'{\\"role\\": \\"reader\\", \\"type\\": \\"user\\", \\"emailAddress\\": \\"manager@company.com\\"}\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-create-feedback-form\\r\\ndescription: \\"Create a Google Form for feedback and share it via Gmail.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-forms\\r\\n        - gws-gmail\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Create and Share a Google Form\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-forms`, `gws-gmail`\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a Google Form for feedback and share it via Gmail.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Create form: `gws forms forms create --json \'{\\"info\\": {\\"title\\": \\"Event Feedback\\", \\"documentTitle\\": \\"Event Feedback Form\\"}}\'`\\r\\n2. Get the form URL from the response (responderUri field)\\r\\n3. Email the form: `gws gmail +send --to attendees@company.com --subject \'Please share your feedback\' --body \'Fill out the form: FORM_URL\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-create-gmail-filter\\r\\ndescription: \\"Create a Gmail filter to automatically label, star, or categorize incoming messages.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-gmail\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Create a Gmail Filter\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-gmail`\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a Gmail filter to automatically label, star, or categorize incoming messages.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. List existing labels: `gws gmail users labels list --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\"}\' --format table`\\r\\n2. Create a new label: `gws gmail users labels create --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\"}\' --json \'{\\"name\\": \\"Receipts\\"}\'`\\r\\n3. Create a filter: `gws gmail users settings filters create --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\"}\' --json \'{\\"criteria\\": {\\"from\\": \\"receipts@example.com\\"}, \\"action\\": {\\"addLabelIds\\": [\\"LABEL_ID\\"], \\"removeLabelIds\\": [\\"INBOX\\"]}}\'`\\r\\n4. Verify filter: `gws gmail users settings filters list --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\"}\' --format table`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-create-meet-space\\r\\ndescription: \\"Create a Google Meet meeting space and share the join link.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"scheduling\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-meet\\r\\n        - gws-gmail\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Create a Google Meet Conference\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-meet`, `gws-gmail`\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a Google Meet meeting space and share the join link.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Create meeting space: `gws meet spaces create --json \'{\\"config\\": {\\"accessType\\": \\"OPEN\\"}}\'`\\r\\n2. Copy the meeting URI from the response\\r\\n3. Email the link: `gws gmail +send --to team@company.com --subject \'Join the meeting\' --body \'Join here: MEETING_URI\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-create-presentation\\r\\ndescription: \\"Create a new Google Slides presentation and add initial slides.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-slides\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Create a Google Slides Presentation\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-slides`\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a new Google Slides presentation and add initial slides.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Create presentation: `gws slides presentations create --json \'{\\"title\\": \\"Quarterly Review Q2\\"}\'`\\r\\n2. Get the presentation ID from the response\\r\\n3. Share with team: `gws drive permissions create --params \'{\\"fileId\\": \\"PRESENTATION_ID\\"}\' --json \'{\\"role\\": \\"writer\\", \\"type\\": \\"user\\", \\"emailAddress\\": \\"team@company.com\\"}\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-create-shared-drive\\r\\ndescription: \\"Create a Google Shared Drive and add members with appropriate roles.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-drive\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Create and Configure a Shared Drive\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-drive`\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a Google Shared Drive and add members with appropriate roles.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Create shared drive: `gws drive drives create --params \'{\\"requestId\\": \\"unique-id-123\\"}\' --json \'{\\"name\\": \\"Project X\\"}\'`\\r\\n2. Add a member: `gws drive permissions create --params \'{\\"fileId\\": \\"DRIVE_ID\\", \\"supportsAllDrives\\": true}\' --json \'{\\"role\\": \\"writer\\", \\"type\\": \\"user\\", \\"emailAddress\\": \\"member@company.com\\"}\'`\\r\\n3. List members: `gws drive permissions list --params \'{\\"fileId\\": \\"DRIVE_ID\\", \\"supportsAllDrives\\": true}\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-create-task-list\\r\\ndescription: \\"Set up a new Google Tasks list with initial tasks.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-tasks\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Create a Task List and Add Tasks\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-tasks`\\r\\n\\r\\nSet up a new Google Tasks list with initial tasks.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Create task list: `gws tasks tasklists insert --json \'{\\"title\\": \\"Q2 Goals\\"}\'`\\r\\n2. Add a task: `gws tasks tasks insert --params \'{\\"tasklist\\": \\"TASKLIST_ID\\"}\' --json \'{\\"title\\": \\"Review Q1 metrics\\", \\"notes\\": \\"Pull data from analytics dashboard\\", \\"due\\": \\"2024-04-01T00:00:00Z\\"}\'`\\r\\n3. Add another task: `gws tasks tasks insert --params \'{\\"tasklist\\": \\"TASKLIST_ID\\"}\' --json \'{\\"title\\": \\"Draft Q2 OKRs\\"}\'`\\r\\n4. List tasks: `gws tasks tasks list --params \'{\\"tasklist\\": \\"TASKLIST_ID\\"}\' --format table`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-create-vacation-responder\\r\\ndescription: \\"Enable a Gmail out-of-office auto-reply with a custom message and date range.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-gmail\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Set Up a Gmail Vacation Responder\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-gmail`\\r\\n\\r\\nEnable a Gmail out-of-office auto-reply with a custom message and date range.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Enable vacation responder: `gws gmail users settings updateVacation --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\"}\' --json \'{\\"enableAutoReply\\": true, \\"responseSubject\\": \\"Out of Office\\", \\"responseBodyPlainText\\": \\"I am out of the office until Jan 20. For urgent matters, contact backup@company.com.\\", \\"restrictToContacts\\": false, \\"restrictToDomain\\": false}\'`\\r\\n2. Verify settings: `gws gmail users settings getVacation --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\"}\'`\\r\\n3. Disable when back: `gws gmail users settings updateVacation --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\"}\' --json \'{\\"enableAutoReply\\": false}\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-draft-email-from-doc\\r\\ndescription: \\"Read content from a Google Doc and use it as the body of a Gmail message.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-docs\\r\\n        - gws-gmail\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Draft a Gmail Message from a Google Doc\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-docs`, `gws-gmail`\\r\\n\\r\\nRead content from a Google Doc and use it as the body of a Gmail message.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Get the document content: `gws docs documents get --params \'{\\"documentId\\": \\"DOC_ID\\"}\'`\\r\\n2. Copy the text from the body content\\r\\n3. Fin…715 tokens truncated…em to another address.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Find labeled messages: `gws gmail users messages list --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\", \\"q\\": \\"label:needs-review\\"}\' --format table`\\r\\n2. Get message content: `gws gmail users messages get --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\", \\"id\\": \\"MSG_ID\\"}\'`\\r\\n3. Forward via new email: `gws gmail +send --to manager@company.com --subject \'FW: [Original Subject]\' --body \'Forwarding for your review:\\r\\n\\r\\n[Original Message Body]\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-generate-report-from-sheet\\r\\ndescription: \\"Read data from a Google Sheet and create a formatted Google Docs report.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-sheets\\r\\n        - gws-docs\\r\\n        - gws-drive\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Generate a Google Docs Report from Sheet Data\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-sheets`, `gws-docs`, `gws-drive`\\r\\n\\r\\nRead data from a Google Sheet and create a formatted Google Docs report.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read the data: `gws sheets +read --spreadsheet SHEET_ID --range \\"Sales!A1:D\\"`\\r\\n2. Create the report doc: `gws docs documents create --json \'{\\"title\\": \\"Sales Report - January 2025\\"}\'`\\r\\n3. Write the report: `gws docs +write --document-id DOC_ID --text \'## Sales Report - January 2025\\r\\n\\r\\n### Summary\\r\\nTotal deals: 45\\r\\nRevenue: $125,000\\r\\n\\r\\n### Top Deals\\r\\n1. Acme Corp - $25,000\\r\\n2. Widget Inc - $18,000\'`\\r\\n4. Share with stakeholders: `gws drive permissions create --params \'{\\"fileId\\": \\"DOC_ID\\"}\' --json \'{\\"role\\": \\"reader\\", \\"type\\": \\"user\\", \\"emailAddress\\": \\"cfo@company.com\\"}\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-label-and-archive-emails\\r\\ndescription: \\"Apply Gmail labels to matching messages and archive them to keep your inbox clean.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-gmail\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Label and Archive Gmail Threads\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-gmail`\\r\\n\\r\\nApply Gmail labels to matching messages and archive them to keep your inbox clean.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Search for matching emails: `gws gmail users messages list --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\", \\"q\\": \\"from:notifications@service.com\\"}\' --format table`\\r\\n2. Apply a label: `gws gmail users messages modify --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\", \\"id\\": \\"MESSAGE_ID\\"}\' --json \'{\\"addLabelIds\\": [\\"LABEL_ID\\"]}\'`\\r\\n3. Archive (remove from inbox): `gws gmail users messages modify --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\", \\"id\\": \\"MESSAGE_ID\\"}\' --json \'{\\"removeLabelIds\\": [\\"INBOX\\"]}\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-log-deal-update\\r\\ndescription: \\"Append a deal status update to a Google Sheets sales tracking spreadsheet.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"sales\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-sheets\\r\\n        - gws-drive\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Log Deal Update to Sheet\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-sheets`, `gws-drive`\\r\\n\\r\\nAppend a deal status update to a Google Sheets sales tracking spreadsheet.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Find the tracking sheet: `gws drive files list --params \'{\\"q\\": \\"name = \'\\\\\'\'Sales Pipeline\'\\\\\'\' and mimeType = \'\\\\\'\'application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet\'\\\\\'\'\\"}\'`\\r\\n2. Read current data: `gws sheets +read --spreadsheet SHEET_ID --range \\"Pipeline!A1:F\\"`\\r\\n3. Append new row: `gws sheets +append --spreadsheet SHEET_ID --range \'Pipeline\' --values \'[\\"2024-03-15\\", \\"Acme Corp\\", \\"Proposal Sent\\", \\"$50,000\\", \\"Q2\\", \\"jdoe\\"]\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-organize-drive-folder\\r\\ndescription: \\"Create a Google Drive folder structure and move files into the right locations.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-drive\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Organize Files into Google Drive Folders\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-drive`\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a Google Drive folder structure and move files into the right locations.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Create a project folder: `gws drive files create --json \'{\\"name\\": \\"Q2 Project\\", \\"mimeType\\": \\"application/vnd.google-apps.folder\\"}\'`\\r\\n2. Create sub-folders: `gws drive files create --json \'{\\"name\\": \\"Documents\\", \\"mimeType\\": \\"application/vnd.google-apps.folder\\", \\"parents\\": [\\"PARENT_FOLDER_ID\\"]}\'`\\r\\n3. Move existing files into folder: `gws drive files update --params \'{\\"fileId\\": \\"FILE_ID\\", \\"addParents\\": \\"FOLDER_ID\\", \\"removeParents\\": \\"OLD_PARENT_ID\\"}\'`\\r\\n4. Verify structure: `gws drive files list --params \'{\\"q\\": \\"FOLDER_ID in parents\\"}\' --format table`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-plan-weekly-schedule\\r\\ndescription: \\"Review your Google Calendar week, identify gaps, and add events to fill them.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"scheduling\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-calendar\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Plan Your Weekly Google Calendar Schedule\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-calendar`\\r\\n\\r\\nReview your Google Calendar week, identify gaps, and add events to fill them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Check this week\'s agenda: `gws calendar +agenda`\\r\\n2. Check free/busy for the week: `gws calendar freebusy query --json \'{\\"timeMin\\": \\"2025-01-20T00:00:00Z\\", \\"timeMax\\": \\"2025-01-25T00:00:00Z\\", \\"items\\": [{\\"id\\": \\"primary\\"}]}\'`\\r\\n3. Add a new event: `gws calendar +insert --summary \'Deep Work Block\' --start \'2026-01-21T14:00:00\' --end \'2026-01-21T16:00:00\'`\\r\\n4. Review updated schedule: `gws calendar +agenda`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-post-mortem-setup\\r\\ndescription: \\"Create a Google Docs post-mortem, schedule a Google Calendar review, and notify via Chat.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"engineering\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-docs\\r\\n        - gws-calendar\\r\\n        - gws-chat\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Set Up Post-Mortem\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-docs`, `gws-calendar`, `gws-chat`\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a Google Docs post-mortem, schedule a Google Calendar review, and notify via Chat.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Create post-mortem doc: `gws docs +write --title \'Post-Mortem: [Incident]\' --body \'## Summary\\\\n\\\\n## Timeline\\\\n\\\\n## Root Cause\\\\n\\\\n## Action Items\'`\\r\\n2. Schedule review meeting: `gws calendar +insert --summary \'Post-Mortem Review: [Incident]\' --attendee team@company.com --start \'2026-03-16T14:00:00\' --end \'2026-03-16T15:00:00\'`\\r\\n3. Notify in Chat: `gws chat +send --space spaces/ENG_SPACE --text \'🔍 Post-mortem scheduled for [Incident].\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-reschedule-meeting\\r\\ndescription: \\"Move a Google Calendar event to a new time and automatically notify all attendees.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"scheduling\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-calendar\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Reschedule a Google Calendar Meeting\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-calendar`\\r\\n\\r\\nMove a Google Calendar event to a new time and automatically notify all attendees.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Find the event: `gws calendar +agenda`\\r\\n2. Get event details: `gws calendar events get --params \'{\\"calendarId\\": \\"primary\\", \\"eventId\\": \\"EVENT_ID\\"}\'`\\r\\n3. Update the time: `gws calendar events patch --params \'{\\"calendarId\\": \\"primary\\", \\"eventId\\": \\"EVENT_ID\\", \\"sendUpdates\\": \\"all\\"}\' --json \'{\\"start\\": {\\"dateTime\\": \\"2025-01-22T14:00:00\\", \\"timeZone\\": \\"America/New_York\\"}, \\"end\\": {\\"dateTime\\": \\"2025-01-22T15:00:00\\", \\"timeZone\\": \\"America/New_York\\"}}\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-review-meet-participants\\r\\ndescription: \\"Review who attended a Google Meet conference and for how long.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-meet\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Review Google Meet Attendance\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-meet`\\r\\n\\r\\nReview who attended a Google Meet conference and for how long.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. List recent conferences: `gws meet conferenceRecords list --format table`\\r\\n2. List participants: `gws meet conferenceRecords participants list --params \'{\\"parent\\": \\"conferenceRecords/CONFERENCE_ID\\"}\' --format table`\\r\\n3. Get session details: `gws meet conferenceRecords participants participantSessions list --params \'{\\"parent\\": \\"conferenceRecords/CONFERENCE_ID/participants/PARTICIPANT_ID\\"}\' --format table`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-review-overdue-tasks\\r\\ndescription: \\"Find Google Tasks that are past due and need attention.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-tasks\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Review Overdue Tasks\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-tasks`\\r\\n\\r\\nFind Google Tasks that are past due and need attention.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. List task lists: `gws tasks tasklists list --format table`\\r\\n2. List tasks with status: `gws tasks tasks list --params \'{\\"tasklist\\": \\"TASKLIST_ID\\", \\"showCompleted\\": false}\' --format table`\\r\\n3. Review due dates and prioritize overdue items\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-save-email-attachments\\r\\ndescription: \\"Find Gmail messages with attachments and save them to a Google Drive folder.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-gmail\\r\\n        - gws-drive\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Save Gmail Attachments to Google Drive\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-gmail`, `gws-drive`\\r\\n\\r\\nFind Gmail messages with attachments and save them to a Google Drive folder.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Get message details: `gws gmail users messages get --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\", \\"id\\": \\"MESSAGE_ID\\"}\'`\\r\\n3. Download attachment: `gws gmail users messages attachments get --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\", \\"messageId\\": \\"MESSAGE_ID\\", \\"id\\": \\"ATTACHMENT_ID\\"}\'`\\r\\n4. Upload to Drive folder: `gws drive +upload --file ./attachment.pdf --parent FOLDER_ID`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-save-email-to-doc\\r\\ndescription: \\"Save a Gmail message body into a Google Doc for archival or reference.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-gmail\\r\\n        - gws-docs\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Save a Gmail Message to Google Docs\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-gmail`, `gws-docs`\\r\\n\\r\\nSave a Gmail message body into a Google Doc for archival or reference.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Find the message: `gws gmail users messages list --params \'{\\"userId\\": \\"me\\", \\"q\\": \\"subject:important from:boss@company.com\\"}\' --format table`\\r\\n2. Write the email body: `gws docs +write --document-id DOC_ID --text \'From: boss@company.com\\r\\nSubject: Important Update\\r\\n\\r\\n[EMAIL BODY]\'`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-schedule-recurring-event\\r\\ndescription: \\"Create a recurring Google Calendar event with attendees.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"scheduling\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-calendar\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Schedule a Recurring Meeting\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-calendar`\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a recurring Google Calendar event with attendees.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Verify it was created: `gws calendar +agenda --days 14 --format table`\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: recipe-send-team-announcement\\r\\ndescription: \\"Send a team announcement via both Gmail and a Google Chat space.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.5\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"recipe\\"\\r\\n    domain: \\"communication\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n      skills:\\r\\n        - gws-gmail\\r\\n        - gws-chat\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Announce via Gmail and Google Chat\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Load the following skills to execute this recipe: `gws-gmail`, `gws-chat`\\r\\n\\r\\nSend a team announcement via both Gmail and a Google Chat space.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1.
