[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 7.5 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"ea2a3b","wall_time_seconds":0.6964934,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":5655,"output":"---\\r\\nname: lsat-u-platform-actions\\r\\ndescription: Perform any LSAT U platform action for Joshua directly from the brain workspace — assign guided drills, homework, or activities; post classroom items and notes; send inbox messages; ingest session notes — by driving the deployed app (lsatprep.study) through his logged-in Chrome admin session, verifying the result, and logging it to the student\'s folder. Trigger on \\"assign <student> …\\", \\"post … to <student>\\", \\"message <student>\\", \\"send <student> homework\\", \\"give <student> an activity\\", or any request to make something happen on the platform from here.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# LSAT U Platform Actions\\r\\n\\r\\nJoshua\'s workplace is this brain workspace, not the app\'s admin UI. This skill makes\\r\\nCodex the operator: he says what should happen to a student on LSAT U, Codex drives\\r\\nthe deployed platform to make it happen, verifies it landed, and records it.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Mechanism\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the **Codex-in-chrome** browser tools against `https://lsatprep.study` with\\r\\nJoshua\'s logged-in Chrome admin session. There is no agent path to the prod Supabase\\r\\nbackend (Lovable-managed, not in MCP scope) — the browser + admin JWT IS the API.\\r\\nDo not insert rows backend-style; act through the same UI flows Joshua would use,\\r\\nunless he explicitly asks for a backend repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n**React controlled-input rule (hard-won 2026-07-16):** `form_input` sets DOM values\\r\\nbut often does NOT update React state, leaving submit buttons silently disabled and\\r\\nproducing zero network traffic. For every form:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Click the field and type with real keystrokes (`computer` type action); for\\r\\n   `<select>`s, click to focus then choose with keyboard (first-letter + Enter) or a\\r\\n   real option click.\\r\\n2. Before clicking submit, confirm the button is actually enabled (full-opacity, or\\r\\n   check `disabled` via read_page).\\r\\n3. After clicking, confirm via `read_network_requests` that the mutation actually\\r\\n   fired (POST to `…supabase.co/functions/v1/…` or `/rest/v1/…`) and returned 2xx.\\r\\n   A UI that merely looks done is not evidence.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Routing — where each action lives\\r\\n\\r\\nAll under `/teacher` (Teacher Desk). Workspaces via `?ws=`: `people` / `students`,\\r\\n`library`, `messages`/`inbox`, `admin`, `gmail`, `drive`.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Action | Surface |\\r\\n|---|---|\\r\\n| Assign a guided drill | `/teacher?ws=library&tab=guided-drills` → drill card → Assign. **Delegate to the `guided-drill-assignment` skill** for selection/QA/logging — it is the specialist; this skill is the router. |\\r\\n| Assign homework / quiz | Teacher Desk library or the student\'s detail page (`TeacherStudentDetail`) → assign flow → creates classroom item + notification |\\r\\n| Assign an activity (e.g. Negation Station) | Library activities surface → Assign; verify resume + notification (see `wiki/tasks.md` activity-centre notes) |\\r\\n| Post a classroom item / note | Student detail page → classroom/dossier tabs |\\r\\n| Message a student | `ws=messages` (admin side of the 1:1 inbox); supports PDF attachments |\\r\\n| Ingest a session transcript | `/teacher/session-ingest` (Phase 1A form: Doc URL + student + optional Gmail message id) or the scan/resolve queue on the same page |\\r\\n| Review/publish a session bundle | Student detail → dossier/review tabs (`SessionBundleReview`); publish is approval-gated |\\r\\n\\r\\nIf a flow\'s exact clicks are unknown, discover them live with read_page/find on the\\r\\nreal surface — do not guess selectors from memory, and do not invent UI that isn\'t\\r\\nthere.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Order of operations (every action)\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Identify the student** exactly (roster names include email; ambiguity → one\\r\\n   concise clarifying question). Check `students/<name>/` for context and\\r\\n   `assignment-log.md` to avoid repeats.\\r\\n2. **Do the action** through the UI per the routing table, honoring the React rule.\\r\\n3. **Verify it landed**: the mutation request returned 2xx AND the UI reflects it\\r\\n   (item appears in the student\'s classroom list / message thread / queue). For\\r\\n   assignments, verify the notification surface where checkable.\\r\\n4. **Log it**: append to `students/<name>/assignment-log.md` (create if missing) with\\r\\n   date, action, item, and evidence; drill verifications also go to\\r\\n   `wiki/guided-drill-verification-log.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Guardrails\\r\\n\\r\\n- Every action here hits **real students on prod**. Anything a student will see\\r\\n  (message text, homework instructions, note bodies) is written in Joshua\'s voice —\\r\\n  route through `wiki/teaching-voice.md`.\\r\\n- If Joshua\'s request fully specifies the action (\\"assign Lydia the conditional\\r\\n  drill\\"), execute without re-asking. If content is open-ended (a message body he\\r\\n  hasn\'t dictated), draft it and show him before sending.\\r\\n- Fail closed: if verification is ambiguous, say exactly what was and wasn\'t\\r\\n  confirmed. Never report an action complete on the strength of a click alone.\\r\\n- No student-facing action as a side effect of a different request.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: lsat-u-architecture\\r\\ndescription: Architectural source of truth and entry point for LSAT U platform rules. Use this skill whenever building, modifying, speccing, or referencing LSAT U platform features. Trigger when discussing component picks, routing, state models, design tokens, drill mechanics, Foyer navigation, Supabase realtime channels, identity/admin patterns, the always-violate rules, or any decision about how LSAT U is built. Also trigger when writing Codex build briefs for LSAT U, when comparing topic modules to the Causation Station architectural template, when explaining LSAT U component patterns, or when reviewing code against platform rules. This skill is the indexed entry point. The canonical full sources live in the vault; this skill gives you the always-violate rules at a glance and routes you to the deeper references. Trigger automatically when Joshua mentions LSAT U code, architecture, components, drill behavior, Foyer, Supabase, build briefs, or topic module integration, even without explicit invocation.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# LSAT U Architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nThis skill is the entry point for LSAT U platform architecture. The canonical full content lives in the Obsidian vault and Joshua\'s memory. This skill gives you the always-violate rules at a glance, the quick decision rules, and explicit pointers to the deeper sources.\\r\\n\\r\\nTreat the vault as source of truth. Treat this skill as the indexed front door.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Always-violate rules (NEVER break these)\\r\\n\\r\\nThese are the daily-use rules. Every contributor follows them without exception. Violating one breaks LSAT U.\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Granular feature flags, not roles.** Permissions are flag-driven, never role-driven. Admin status is a flag, not a role.\\r\\n2. **Admin always displays as \\"Joshua\\"** via `displayName.ts`. Never expose the underlying account identifier in UI.\\r\\n3. **No bottom dock.** Foyer is the navigation surface. Do not add a bottom dock anywhere.\\r\\n4. **Drill is always dark mode** with cleanup restore on exit. Other surfaces follow user preference. Drill is fixed dark.\\r\\n5. **1:1 messaging only** between admin and student. No group, no broadcast.\\r\\n6. **Zero layout shift highlighting.** Use `box-decoration-break: clone`. Highlights never reflow content.\\r\\n7. **SVG ring not Canvas** for the Foyer hero (`radial-orbital-timeline.tsx`). Canvas is banned for that surface.\\r\\n8. **Postgres-side provisioning** for new users and resources (post Issue #7). Application-side provisioning is removed.\\r\\n9. **Deterministic channel names** for Supabase realtime. No random IDs in channel names.\\r\\n10. **DB mutations never swallow errors.** Every mutation surfaces failure to the user or rethrows.\\r\\n11. **Causation Station is the architectural template** for all topic modules. Inherit its patterns. Do not invent new patterns per topic.\\r\\n12. **Topic modules are repo-native, not standalone.** No separate apps, no separate hosting. Topic modules live inside the LSAT U repo and share its routing, auth, components.\\r\\n\\r\\n## When in doubt (quick decision rules)\\r\\n\\r\\n- Granular flag or role? **Flag.**\\r\\n- New nav surface or Foyer? **Foyer.**\\r\\n- Drill light mode or dark? **Dark.**\\r\\n- Custom component or library? **Library, unless impossible.**\\r\\n- Swallow the error or rethrow? **Rethrow.**\\r\\n- Topic module standalone or repo-native? **Repo-native.**\\r\\n- Random channel ID or deterministic? **Deterministic.**\\r\\n- Application-side or Postgres-side provisioning? **Postgres.**\\r\\n- Canvas or SVG for the Foyer ring? **SVG.**\\r\\n- Invent a new pattern or inherit Causation Station? **Inherit.**\\r\\n\\r\\n## Canonical sources (read these for deeper context)\\r\\n\\r\\nFor anything beyond the daily-use rules above, route to the canonical content. Authority order when sources conflict, from highest to lowest:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Live repo `~/ai-os/projects/lsatu/`**. Code is ground truth when documentation drifts.\\r\\n2. **April 2026 audit bundle `~/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/sources/april-2026-audit.md/`**. 14 files documenting verified bugs (F-IDs), the schema drift chain, audit corrections, persistence layer status. Entry points: `PLAYBOOK.md`, `master-reference.md`, `00-index.md`.\\r\\n3. **Vault `~/ai-os/AGENTS.md`**. Architecture rules section plus curriculum/pedagogy rules.\\r\\n4. **Joshua\'s memory, edit #4** (\\"LSAT U architecture rules, never violate\\"). Short reminder list.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you find a contradiction between sources, fix the lower-authority source, not the higher one.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tech stack (quick reference)\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Frontend:** React 18, Vite 5, TypeScript (`strict: false`, do not rely on type safety), Tailwind 3.4, shadcn/ui, motion/react\\r\\n- **Component primitives:** @base-ui/react\\r\\n- **Backend:** Supabase, project ID `qodidbkoqrmqhdfwvcmk`\\r\\n- **Hosting:** Lovable, auto-deploy from GitHub\\r\\n- **Build:** SWC, no type checking at build time\\r\\n\\r\\nDeeper repo and config details live in the audit bundle and the live repo itself.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Foyer pattern (the nav surface)\\r\\n\\r\\nThree-surface architecture:\\r\\n- **Sidebar:** `FoyerSidebar.tsx`\\r\\n- **Orbital ring (hero):** `radial-orbital-timeline.tsx`. Three nodes: SMART DRILL, FIND, RESUME. SVG, not Canvas.\\r\\n- **Dock:** `FoyerDock.tsx`\\r\\n\\r\\nTopic modules route from Foyer. Never add a bottom dock.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Component library\\r\\n\\r\\n27 components, indexed at `~/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/components/_INDEX.md`. Categories: primitives, forms, overlays, animation, backgrounds, marketing, chat. Pick from this library first. Custom warranted only when the existing library cannot teach the topic mechanic.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Bug ID conventions\\r\\n\\r\\nLSAT U bugs use F-prefix IDs (F2.13, F4.1, etc.). The April 2026 audit bundle is canonical. Reference F-IDs in any code change that fixes a known issue. See `raw/lsat-u-audit-2026-04/06-cross-scan-verification.md` for verified IDs.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What this skill is NOT for\\r\\n\\r\\n- Writing student-facing content. Use `lsat-u-voice` for that.\\r\\n- Curriculum decisions about what to teach. Use the curriculum build pipeline.\\r\\n- Source teaching material analysis. Out of scope.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Maintenance\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen canonical decisions change in the vault or repo, update this skill\'s always-violate list and when-in-doubt rules to match. The pointers to canonical sources stay stable. The daily-use rules drift, so they live here for fast access.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: lsatu-cc-handoff\\r\\ndescription: Operational skill for the LSAT U build loop. Trigger whenever Joshua is working on the LSAT U codebase and needs to translate a UI screenshot, complaint, idea, or bug into a Codex execution prompt. Also trigger on phrases like \\"send to CC,\\" \\"paste box,\\" \\"create a CC handoff,\\" \\"fix this and send to terminal,\\" \\"make a CC prompt,\\" \\"send this to Codex,\\" or whenever Joshua sends a screenshot of lsatprep.study or the lovable.dev preview with a complaint or change request. The skill enforces the analyze then write-brief-to-vault then give-paste-box pattern, the file path conventions, the hard rules (no em dashes, verbatim content, brutalist palette, no silent errors, direct commits), and Joshua\'s voice rules (terse, opinionated, no em dashes, modules not phases). This skill is the indexed front door for the build loop. The deeper rules live in LSATU memory and the lsat-u-architecture skill.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# LSAT U Build Loop: Codex Handoff\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is the operational skill for translating Joshua\'s input into a Codex execution prompt. Use it every time the loop runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe loop: input -> analyze -> write brief to vault -> hand paste box back to Joshua -> CC executes -> Joshua returns with results.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 1: Analyze before writing\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore writing a single line of brief, do all of the following:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Read the actual current code.** Do not write recommendations from memory. The LSATU repo is at `~/ai-os/projects/lsatu/`. The topic modules live in `src/topics/<topic>/`. Read the relevant view files, data files, and store files before recommending changes.\\r\\n\\r\\n2. **Read the existing vault docs.** Curriculum work lives in `~/ai-os/raw/sources/lsat-u/curriculum/<topic>/`. Look for `_BUILD_SPEC*.md`, `MODULE_PLAN.md`, `_HANDOFF/`, `_source/`, `_archive/`. Existing briefs that contradict the new direction must be archived (move to `_archive/`).\\r\\n\\r\\n3. **Verify content authenticity.** Joshua authors the LSAT curriculum. Codex does not invent LSAT content. When auditing quiz files, drill banks, or lesson body content, check whether items are verbatim from `_source/` files or from git history (e.g. `git show <sha>:<path>`), or if they were fabricated by a prior Codex run. Flag fabrications to a `_CONTENT_AUDIT.md` rather than silently rewriting.\\r\\n\\r\\n4. **If a screenshot was provided.** Describe what is visible. List specific visual problems with concrete CSS-class-level fixes. Cross-reference against the rendering component (LessonBody.tsx, ModuleView.tsx, the per-quiz renderers) to identify the root cause.\\r\\n\\r\\n5. **Push back where appropriate.** If Joshua\'s stated direction will introduce complexity (adding features, more sidebar entries, more drill types, more chrome), say so. The bootcamp default is simpler-not-more. Brutalist preservation is non-negotiable but everything else should reduce cognitive load.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 2: Write the build brief to vault\\r\\n\\r\\nFile path convention: `~/ai-os/raw/sources/lsat-u/curriculum/<topic>/<BRIEF_NAME>.md`\\r\\n\\r\\nName patterns Joshua uses:\\r\\n- `MODULE_PLAN.md` (architecture-defining)\\r\\n- `<DOMAIN>_<ACTION>.md` like `LESSON_READABILITY_FIX.md`, `MODULE_QUALITY_UPGRADE.md`, `MODULE_CLOSEOUT.md`\\r\\n- `_AUDIT_<DATE>.md` for audit findings\\r\\n- `_HANDOFF/<NN>_<NAME>_BRIEF.md` only if Joshua already has that subfolder convention going\\r\\n\\r\\n**Required sections in every brief:**\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Frontmatter line: `For: Codex`, `Direct commits to main. Push after each step.`\\r\\n2. Goal: one or two sentences.\\r\\n3. Required reading: explicit list of files CC must read before writing code. Always includes the brief itself, the relevant view files, the architecture spec (`_BUILD_SPEC_v2.0.md` or `MODULE_PLAN.md`), and `~/ai-os/AGENTS.md`.\\r\\n4. Hard rules. Always include:\\r\\n   - No em dashes. `grep -rn \'—\' src/topics/<topic>/` must return zero before push.\\r\\n   - Verbatim curriculum content. Do not paraphrase walkthroughs, vocab callouts, worked examples, or LSAT stimuli.\\r\\n   - Brutalist palette preserved. Same `brutal-*` tokens. Same `.topic-abstract` wrapper.\\r\\n   - Every Supabase mutation returns `{ ok, error }`. No silent errors. Errors surface as toasts.\\r\\n   - No `(supabase as any)`. Regenerate types if schema changes.\\r\\n   - Direct commits to main. Push at the end of each step.\\r\\n   - Do not invent LSAT content. Stop and ask if a source is missing.\\r\\n5. Numbered steps. Always called \\"Step 1, Step 2, ...\\" not \\"Phase 1, Phase 2.\\" Joshua dislikes the word \\"phase.\\"\\r\\n6. Per step: target files, what changes, expected outcome, commit message.\\r\\n7. Verification block: explicit checklist for the final push (em dash check, build, dev walk, mobile viewport, reduced motion, keyboard-only when relevant).\\r\\n8. Done-state report template using fenced code block with `DONE:` header, commits list, verification checks, open issues.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Brief length target:** 100 to 250 lines. Tight. Concrete. No filler.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Archive superseded briefs.** When a new brief replaces a prior plan in the same domain, move the old one to `_archive/<NAME>_superseded.md`. The vault stays clean.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 3: Hand the paste box back to Joshua\\r\\n\\r\\nAfter the brief is saved, give Joshua a paste-box prompt as a markdown code block. The prompt must:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reference the brief by full vault path with `~/Documents/Obsidian\\\\ Vault/...` (escape the space).\\r\\n2. Tell CC to \\"execute end to end. Commit and push after each step.\\"\\r\\n3. Restate the hard rules in one short paragraph.\\r\\n4. List the steps in one-line summaries.\\r\\n5. Note any migrations or external actions required (e.g., \\"Apply migration via Supabase dashboard if CLI not linked\\").\\r\\n6. End with: \\"If a step blocks, stop and post status. Otherwise run all N steps and post the done-state report. Go.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n**The paste-box format is the deliverable Joshua actually uses.** It must be inside a single fenced code block so he can copy with one click. No surrounding commentary inside the code block.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 4: Voice and tone rules when writing to Joshua\\r\\n\\r\\n- No em dashes anywhere. Use colons, periods, or restructure.\\r\\n- Terse. Direct. Strong opinionated recommendations, not hedged suggestions.\\r\\n- Push back when Joshua\'s direction would introduce complexity or break existing rules.\\r\\n- Skills-check rule: before creating, modifying, or recommending any skill, read `~/ai-os/raw/sources/lsat-u/skills-reference/00_skills-strategy.md` and `01_skills-detailed-evaluation.md` first. Conform to documented patterns.\\r\\n- Modules not phases.\\r\\n- Don\'t repeat what already shipped. Just acknowledge and move on.\\r\\n- Don\'t ask multiple-choice questions when Joshua has given clear autonomy. Make the call, document it, move.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Common brief types\\r\\n\\r\\n**Audit brief** — finding gaps in shipped work. Output: `_AUDIT_<DATE>.md` plus a follow-up fix brief.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Build brief** — implementing new feature or major restructure. Output: `<DOMAIN>_PLAN.md` or `<DOMAIN>_<FEATURE>.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Fix brief** — closing specific bugs or visual issues. Output: `<DOMAIN>_FIX.md` or `<DOMAIN>_READABILITY_FIX.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Closeout brief** — finishing items left open by a prior pass. Output: `<DOMAIN>_CLOSEOUT.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Cleanup brief** — removing zombies, archiving superseded files, regenerating types. Output: `<DOMAIN>_CLEANUP.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Anti-patterns to avoid\\r\\n\\r\\n- Writing a brief without reading the current code first.\\r\\n- Using \\"Phase 1, Phase 2\\" language. Always \\"Step 1, Step 2\\" or \\"Module 1, Module 2.\\"\\r\\n- Adding more sidebar entries when the conversation context is \\"simplify.\\"\\r\\n- Including em dashes in vault docs or paste boxes.\\r\\n- Writing paste boxes that span multiple code blocks or include surrounding prose inside the fenced block.\\r\\n- Inventing LSAT content. Joshua writes the curriculum.\\r\\n- Skipping the archive step when a brief supersedes prior work.\\r\\n- Asking multiple questions when Joshua has said \\"take autonomy\\" or \\"just do it.\\"\\r\\n- Putting the brief in `/mnt/user-data/outputs/` or anywhere outside the vault. Vault path is the source of truth.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Pointers to deeper sources\\r\\n\\r\\n- LSATU architecture rules: `C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/skills/lsat-u-architecture/SKILL.md`\\r\\n- LSATU repo: `~/ai-os/projects/lsatu/`\\r\\n- Abstract bootcamp vault: `~/ai-os/raw/sources/lsat-u/curriculum/Abstract/`\\r\\n- Skills strategy: `~/ai-os/raw/sources/lsat-u/skills-reference/00_skills-strategy.md`\\r\\n- Codex folder system: `~/ai-os/projects/`, `~/ai-os/raw/sources/lsat-u/prompts/`, `~/ai-os/raw/inbox/chat-exports/`, `~/ai-os/archive/`\\r\\n- Cowork prompts: `~/ai-os/raw/sources/lsat-u/prompts/`\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen in doubt about a convention, check the lsat-u-architecture skill or the Abstract vault for an existing example. Then conform.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: pull-submissions\\r\\ndescription: Pull booking-time student submissions (files + comments) from the LSAT U backend into students/<name>/submissions/. Use when Joshua says \\"pull submissions\\", \\"get the booking uploads\\", \\"sync student submissions\\", or as part of /pickup. On-demand only — no cron, no watcher.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Pull Submissions\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen a student books a session through their `/book/<slug>` link, the confirm step lets them optionally attach work (any file, up to 5) and leave a comment. Those land in the LSAT U backend (Supabase storage + `external_work_uploads`, comment on `booking_pass_redemptions.student_note`) and are surfaced in the Bookings admin tab and the booking confirmation email to Joshua.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis skill is the **on-demand pull** that mirrors those submissions into the ai-os brain, so a student\'s work lives alongside their transcripts.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What it does\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Logs in with the admin creds in `~/ai-os/.env` (`LSATPREP_ADMIN_*`) against GoTrue, exactly as the admin UI authenticates.\\r\\n2. Calls `booking-pass-admin` → `list_bookings`, keeps every booking that has a note or attached files.\\r\\n3. For each new one, downloads the files (via short-lived signed URLs from `get_booking_uploads`) and writes the comment, into `students/<name>/submissions/`.\\r\\n4. Records each pulled redemption in a per-student `.pulled.json` manifest so re-running only fetches what\'s new (idempotent).\\r\\n\\r\\n## Run it\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nbash ~/ai-os/skills/Codex/pull-submissions/pull-submissions.sh            # pull everything new\\r\\nbash ~/ai-os/skills/Codex/pull-submissions/pull-submissions.sh --dry-run  # list only, write nothing\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nRequires `curl` and `jq`. Reads `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` / `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` from `projects/lsatu/.env` and the admin creds from the root `.env` (both sourced with absolute paths — cwd is unreliable).\\r\\n\\r\\n## Output layout\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nstudents/<name>/submissions/\\r\\n  .pulled.json                       # manifest of redemption ids already pulled\\r\\n  2026-07-19_a1b2c3d4_note.md        # the student\'s comment (if any)\\r\\n  2026-07-19_a1b2c3d4_PT155.pdf      # each attached file, prefixed date_redemption\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nStudent name → folder slug is derived from the pass name (lowercased, hyphenated). If the folder doesn\'t exist yet it\'s created; reconcile a new folder against `students/README.md` naming if the student already has a record under a different slug.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Notes\\r\\n\\r\\n- On-demand by design. Do not add a cron or launchd watcher — Joshua decided the pull is manual (can run inside `/pickup`).\\r\\n- The backend is the source of truth; this is a mirror. Never delete backend rows from here.\\r\\n- Files download through 10-minute signed URLs; if a download 403s, just re-run (a fresh URL is minted each call).\\r\\n"}'}]

[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 6.4 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"18d2da","wall_time_seconds":0.5343972,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":5605,"output":"---\\r\\nname: ingest\\r\\ndescription: >\\r\\n  The single front door for adding sources to the current knowledge base. Use\\r\\n  for \\"ingest this\\", \\"process this source\\", \\"file these notes\\", \\"add this to\\r\\n  my second brain\\", \\"ingest the latest clips\\", or a supplied document meant\\r\\n  to become saved knowledge. Finds the input, checks content hashes, preserves\\r\\n  provenance, and compiles it into linked wiki pages. Session write-ups and\\r\\n  student-facing post-session recaps belong to lsat-session-lesson.\\r\\nallowed-tools: Bash Read Write Edit Glob Grep\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Ingest sources into the current brain\\r\\n\\r\\nOne public skill owns discovery, duplicate checks, preservation, routing, and\\r\\nwiki compilation. `second-brain-ingest` is a compatibility name for this same\\r\\nworkflow, not another pipeline. Read the internal\\r\\n`references/wiki-compilation.md` when processing knowledge sources.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Resolve the vault and schema first\\r\\n\\r\\nFind the vault root from the current workspace and its nearest instruction files.\\r\\nRead `system/schema/llm-wiki.md` relative to that root. It is the authority for\\r\\nfolder conventions, page metadata, provenance, index, log, and ingest/query/lint\\r\\nworkflows. Do not assume a saved Windows or Mac path. If no schema exists in the\\r\\ntarget vault, report that gap before changing its structure; never initialize a\\r\\nsecond vault to solve a request about an existing one.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Route first\\r\\n\\r\\nIdentify what is being ingested, then jump to that section. If it is genuinely\\r\\nambiguous, ask once. Do not guess and file it somewhere wrong.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Input | Where it lands | Section |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| Web clip from Obsidian Web Clipper (`.md` in `raw/inbox/`) | `raw/inbox/` | [Clips](#clips) |\\r\\n| A clip that is a YouTube / video page | `raw/inbox/` | [Clips](#clips), read via `watch` |\\r\\n| Gemini \\"Notes by Gemini\\" from a live session (this week, last week) | Google Drive | [Transcripts, live](#transcripts-live) |\\r\\n| Archival Gemini `.docx` / `.txt` (Apr to Jul 2026 Takeout batch) | `raw/data-about-me/transcripts/` | [Transcripts, archival](#transcripts-archival) |\\r\\n| Superwhisper `recordings/` dirs (`meta.json` + `output.wav`) or `settings.json` | wherever they were dropped | hand to `superwhisper`; not this skill\'s |\\r\\n| Student evidence: PT score report, screenshot, homework export | `~/Downloads`, chat attachment | [Student evidence](#student-evidence) |\\r\\n| A source document meant to become wiki knowledge | `raw/` | dedupe below, then read `references/wiki-compilation.md` |\\r\\n| Takeout or platform dump | `raw/data-about-me/` | [Bulk exports](#bulk-exports) |\\r\\n\\r\\nKnowledge-source compilation is this skill\'s internal reference. `lsat-session-lesson`\\r\\nowns the complete student-facing session write-up workflow. A request only to\\r\\nretrieve or file a transcript stays narrow; a recap request goes directly to that\\r\\nskill without asking for a second activation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Always, before any pipeline\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Find the file without asking where it is.** Search newest-first:\\r\\n   ```\\r\\n   raw/inbox/   raw/sources/   ~/Downloads/   ~/Desktop/   students/*/transcript-downloads/\\r\\n   ```\\r\\n   Ask only if that comes up empty. He has answered \\"where is it\\" too many\\r\\n   times. `raw/inbox/` is the single intake queue; the old top-level\\r\\n   `Clippings/` folder was folded into `raw/sources/clips/` on 2026-09-08, so a\\r\\n   `Clippings/` path in an old note is stale.\\r\\n2. **Dedupe by SHA-256, not by name.** On Windows use `Get-FileHash` or\\r\\n   Python `hashlib`. Check existing archive manifests, source-page metadata,\\r\\n   and dated ingest entries. A matching filename alone is not proof. A matching\\r\\n   hash with completed wiki output means report the existing output and stop.\\r\\n   An archived hash without finished output means resume compilation, not\\r\\n   discard the source. Never delete duplicates.\\r\\n3. **Check the log and source summary.** Record whether the candidate was\\r\\n   previously processed and whether this is a new revision. Preserve both\\r\\n   generations when content changed. A deliberate re-ingest updates the\\r\\n   existing source page with revision provenance, not a duplicate truth.\\r\\n4. **Preserve the input byte-for-byte.** Copy external attachments or inbox\\r\\n   inputs to an appropriate `raw/sources/` archive and verify the SHA-256 before\\r\\n   citing the preserved copy. Record origin, URL/author/date when known,\\r\\n   capture date, archived date, filename, size, and hash. Do not move, delete,\\r\\n   overwrite, or edit original source bytes. Do not follow symlinks outside a\\r\\n   registered source root. Existing archived inputs can be read in place.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Clips\\r\\n\\r\\nObsidian Web Clipper writes `.md` files to `raw/inbox/`. Anything else sitting\\r\\nthere (a `recordings/` tree, a `settings.json`) is not a clip; route it by the\\r\\ntable above and tell Joshua it was in the wrong place rather than processing it\\r\\nhere.\\r\\n\\r\\n1. List `raw/inbox/*.md` newest-first. \\"The latest\\" means the newest; a named\\r\\n   topic means match on it; several new ones means list them and ask which.\\r\\n2. Dedupe (above).\\r\\n3. Read the clip fully. If it is a video page with no transcript, use the\\r\\n   appropriate transcript intake workflow; do not treat its thumbnail as evidence.\\r\\n4. Copy and hash-verify the clip into `raw/sources/clips/<slug>/`, using\\r\\n   `PROVENANCE.md` and `SHA256SUMS`. Reuse an existing identical archive.\\r\\n   Preserve the inbox original. Processed status comes from its hash, source\\r\\n   page, and log, not from whether the original still exists in the inbox.\\r\\n5. Follow `references/wiki-compilation.md` through the source summary,\\r\\n   relevant existing pages, index update, log entry, and verification.\\r\\n\\r\\nOne source at a time unless Joshua explicitly asks for batch work. Discuss\\r\\nimportant takeaways as part of the work. An explicit instruction to implement,\\r\\nfile, or ingest with a stated focus authorizes completing that scope; do not\\r\\nintroduce an extra confirmation step. Ask when unresolved emphasis, identity,\\r\\nor contradictory evidence materially changes what should be written.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Transcripts, live\\r\\n\\r\\nGemini writes \\"Notes by Gemini\\" docs to Google Drive after each Meet session.\\r\\nThe brain\'s copy is `students/<slug>/transcript-downloads/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>-notes-by-gemini.md`\\r\\n(primary record: the brain is its only home). Getting them there is step 1 of\\r\\n`lsat-session-lesson/references/transcript-intake-and-record.md`; follow that section exactly (Calendar sweep by guest email,\\r\\nDrive sweep for unattached docs, export as `text/plain`, resolve the person\\r\\nwith `students/_aliases.md`, consultations and unknowns to\\r\\n`students/_other-sessions/`). It is the single source of truth for the pull;\\r\\ndo not re-derive the `gws` commands here.\\r\\n\\r\\nThen, per transcript that is new on disk:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read the whole transcript, not the Gemini summary at the top. The summary\\r\\n   flattens what the student actually did; the distillation has to name the\\r\\n   answer they picked and the line they misread.\\r\\n2. Append to the student\'s `teaching-notes.md` (create it from a sibling if the\\r\\n   folder lacks one; it is a standard primary file): what was taught, where they\\r\\n   struggled, what was assigned, what to follow up. Dated heading, append-only,\\r\\n   never regenerate.\\r\\n3. Anything needing an action goes to `open-loops.md` (same rules).\\r\\n4. Add one line to `transcripts.md` so the folder\'s inventory matches disk.\\r\\n5. Never write to a `*.generated.md` file; those mirror a live backend.\\r\\n6. Append to `wiki/log.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\nDone means every session in the window either has its transcript on disk and\\r\\ndistilled, or is listed in the log as \\"no Gemini doc anywhere\\" with the date and\\r\\nstudent, so the next session does not sweep it again.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf Joshua requests a session write-up or recap, activate `lsat-session-lesson`\\r\\nand complete its workflow; do not stop at telling him another skill is needed.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Transcripts, archival\\r\\n\\r\\nThe Takeout batch of 52 `.docx` / `.txt` files in `raw/data-about-me/transcripts/`\\r\\n(2026-04-28 to 2026-07-15) was distilled on 2026-07-20 (`wiki/log.md`). It is\\r\\ngit-ignored PII; never read the folder wholesale into context.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Start with the inventory. Do not re-derive the mapping by hand.**\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\npython system/scripts/transcript-inventory.py              # full report\\r\\npython system/scripts/transcript-inventory.py --unmatched  # only the gaps\\r\\npython system/scripts/transcript-inventory.py --json       # machine-readable\\r\\npython system/scripts/transcript-inventory.py --text \\"<file>.docx\\"   # one transcript as text\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIt maps each file to a folder using `students/_aliases.md`, knows that former\\r\\nstudents live in `students/non-students/`, and prints what it cannot resolve.\\r\\n`--text` exists because this box has no python-docx and no pandoc; it is how a\\r\\n`.docx` gets read. The script is read-only.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor an unmapped file, resolve before filing:\\r\\n- a name variant of an existing student: add it under `## Aliases` in\\r\\n  `students/_aliases.md`, re-run, continue;\\r\\n- a consultation or one-off: add under `## Prospects, no record yet` (the\\r\\n  section the script parses) so it stops surfacing;\\r\\n- a real recurring student with no folder: **ask Joshua before creating one.**\\r\\n  A folder is a judgment about the relationship, not a filing detail.\\r\\n\\r\\nThen distill exactly as in the live section, steps 1 to 6. The `.docx` stays in\\r\\n`raw/`; what lands in the student folder is what a human wants to read before\\r\\nthe next session.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the inventory gets a mapping wrong, fix the script or the alias file. Working\\r\\naround it silently means the next session re-derives the same mapping.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Student evidence\\r\\n\\r\\nPT score reports, intake screenshots, homework exports, anything about one\\r\\nstudent that arrives as a file.\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Identify the student (filename, chat context, contents). Ask if unclear.\\r\\n2. Dedupe (above).\\r\\n3. Copy into the student folder under the matching standard subfolder from\\r\\n   `students/README.md`: score reports to `Practice_Test_Reports/`, assigned\\r\\n   work to `Student_Specific_Homework/`, otherwise the folder root with a dated\\r\\n   name. These are raw evidence: read for diagnosis, never edited.\\r\\n4. If it changes a judgment, append the judgment to `teaching-notes.md` with the\\r\\n   file as its cited source.\\r\\n5. Log it.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Bulk exports\\r\\n\\r\\nTakeout and platform dumps land in `raw/data-about-me/` and are git-ignored PII.\\r\\n\\r\\n- Never read one wholesale; it has blown the context window before.\\r\\n- Inventory first (file counts, types, date ranges), report, and let Joshua\\r\\n  pick what matters.\\r\\n- Duplicate exports are common and large. Report duplicates by hash and size;\\r\\n  do not delete without asking.\\r\\n- Analysis across many files goes to a sub-agent that returns a summary, not\\r\\n  file contents.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Hard rules\\r\\n\\r\\n- Never move, delete, or modify original sources. Preserve revisions and hashes.\\r\\n- Never create a student folder without resolving the relationship with Joshua.\\r\\n- Never hand-edit `*.generated.md`; use its owning generator.\\r\\n- Dedupe before ingesting. Distinguish archived from successfully compiled.\\r\\n- Process one source at a time unless batch work is explicitly requested.\\r\\n- Government IDs stay outside this OS. Do not ingest them.\\r\\n- Use the current machine\'s tools and paths, resolved from the vault root.\\r\\n- No email, platform publishing, or assignment is implied by local ingestion.\\r\\n- Read current target contents before changing pages. Automated writes only\\r\\n  modify generated files or fenced generated sections and compare their expected\\r\\n  hash before writing; on a mismatch, re-read and merge instead of overwriting.\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: level-up\\r\\ndescription: Use when someone asks to level up their AIOS, close an audit gap, find what to automate next, or improve one workflow. Walks the 3Ms from choosing the constraint to shipping one useful artifact or verified repair.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n> *Adapted from The Three Ms of AI™. © 2026 Nate Herk. All rights reserved.*\\r\\n> *The Three Ms of AI™ is a trademark of Nate Herk.*\\r\\n\\r\\n## What this skill does\\r\\n\\r\\nWalks the user through the 3Ms each week to surface and ship one new automation. **One interview = one artifact.** It also installs the 3Ms framework into the user\'s head over time — after 4-6 runs, the user starts spotting opportunities mid-week without prompting because the questions have become internal defaults.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is the brain-rewire mechanism. The kit doesn\'t need cron jobs to anchor behavior; it needs `/level-up` running every Friday.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What `/level-up` is NOT\\r\\n\\r\\n- Not `/audit`. `/audit` is structural (\\"is the AIOS built right?\\"). `/level-up` is functional (\\"what business leverage am I missing?\\"). Run `/audit` first if structure is messy.\\r\\n- Not a multi-candidate planner. One run = one shipped artifact.\\r\\n- Not a coach. The user does the thinking. The skill conducts the interview.\\r\\n\\r\\n## When `/level-up` runs\\r\\n\\r\\n- **First run: Day 14.** After the user has connected ≥1 MCP/script and run `/audit` once. Earlier yields trivial output.\\r\\n- **Cadence: weekly, Friday afternoon.** Review the week, surface one automation, ship Monday.\\r\\n- **On-demand any time.** Mid-week if a manual task itches.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Inputs the skill reads\\r\\n\\r\\nFirst read the applicable operating manual. The paths below are starter-kit defaults: resolve priorities, identity, and connections through the current project\'s declared routes when it uses different locations. Do not create duplicate context files because these defaults are absent. Use `references/3ms-framework.md` if present; otherwise read the bundled [3Ms framework](references/3ms-framework.md). Ask only for information unavailable in the existing sources.\\r\\n\\r\\n- `context/priorities.md` — what the user said matters\\r\\n- `context/about-me.md` — top_pain, role\\r\\n- `connections.md` — what\'s reachable, by what mechanism\\r\\n- `references/3ms-framework.md` — the framework (used to quote principles back)\\r\\n- `decisions/log.md` — recent decisions (what\'s already shipped or considered)\\r\\n- `.Codex/skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter — what capabilities exist\\r\\n- Recent `audits/audit-{date}.md` if present\\r\\n\\r\\n## Execution — three phases\\r\\n\\r\\n### Coming from an audit\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the user supplies an `/audit` finding or a recent report is available, carry its evidence, affected route/workflow, and completion check into Phase 1. Use that gap as the first candidate; ask only for missing context instead of restarting a generic interview. Do not chase points or assume an unverified connection is broken.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor a routing-only fix, use `/link` when available and the user has requested the edit. For a selected workflow repair, improve that existing workflow rather than creating a duplicate skill. A verified repair counts as the one artifact for this run. Preserve the Method reasoning, relevant scope/permissions, and validation steps. A practical measure can be fewer failed retrievals, fewer missed runs, or less time finding a source.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor repairs, skip creation-only scaffolding. The scaffold headers below apply to new workflow artifacts, never to operating manuals or routing indexes.\\r\\n\\r\\nClose with the repair\'s acceptance evidence and recommend `/audit` again. Do not claim a higher score until the new audit verifies it; repeated-use and due-run evidence must accumulate through actual use.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Phase 1 — Mindset interview (find the candidate)\\r\\n\\r\\nSurface 1-3 candidates ranked by leverage. Ask these in order, conversationally:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. *\\"Walk me through your week. What did you do 3+ times?\\"* (frequency)\\r\\n2. *\\"Anything that felt manual, boring, or copy-paste?\\"* (drudgery)\\r\\n3. *\\"Anything where you thought \'a smart intern could handle this\'?\\"* (delegation)\\r\\n4. *\\"If 500 new clients showed up tomorrow, what would break first?\\"* (constraint)\\r\\n5. *\\"What would give you 500 more clients tomorrow?\\"* (growth lever)\\r\\n\\r\\nQuote relevant Mindset principles when they fit:\\r\\n- *\\"Sounds like the Default Shift applies — to what extent could AI be leveraged here?\\"*\\r\\n- *\\"This is the Function Breakdown — you\'re not automating the whole job, just this one piece.\\"*\\r\\n- *\\"AI is better than you think and improving faster than you think. If it couldn\'t do this last quarter, it might be ready now.\\"*\\r\\n\\r\\n**Output of Phase 1:** numbered list of 1-3 candidate opportunities, one-line \\"why this is leverage\\" per candidate. Ask: *\\"Pick one to scope.\\"*\\r\\n\\r\\n### Phase 2 — Method interview (scope one)\\r\\n\\r\\nUser picks one candidate. Walk the 5-step Method pipeline:\\r\\n\\r\\n**Step 1 — Find the constraint.** Which bottleneck does this solve, or which growth lever does it open? Tie back to Phase 1 answers.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Step 2 — EAD: Eliminate / Automate / Delegate.**\\r\\n- **Eliminate first:** *\\"What happens if we just stop doing this?\\"* If the answer is \\"nothing breaks\\" → skill exits cheerfully. *\\"Don\'t automate waste.\\"* This is a win, log to `decisions/log.md` and stop.\\r\\n- **Automate second:** apply 60/30/10 framing. ~60% deterministic, ~30% AI-assisted, ~10% manual.\\r\\n- **Delegate third:** if too complex/variable/judgment-heavy → suggest a person. Skill exits with a delegation suggestion, log it.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Step 3 — Map the process.** Five elements:\\r\\n- Trigger (what kicks it off)\\r\\n- Data sources (where info comes from)\\r\\n- Data transformations (how data changes shape)\\r\\n- Decision points (where it branches)\\r\\n- Destination (where output goes)\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the user can\'t articulate any of the five: *\\"If you can\'t explain it to a person, you can\'t explain it to an AI. Sketch it on paper first, then come back.\\"* Skill stops.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Step 4 — Pick the autonomy level.**\\r\\n\\r\\n| Level | Name | What happens |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| L0 | Manual | No AI |\\r\\n| L1 | Suggested | AI suggests, human decides every step |\\r\\n| L2 | Drafted | AI drafts, human reviews and edits |\\r\\n| L3 | Supervised | AI runs, human validates periodically |\\r\\n| L4 | Autonomous | AI handles end-to-end |\\r\\n\\r\\n**Default = lowest level that solves the problem.** Push back on L4 unless the user has explicitly run lower levels first. *\\"Workflows beat agents. If a decision doesn\'t HAVE to be made by AI, don\'t let AI make it.\\"*\\r\\n\\r\\n**Step 5 — Tie to a KPI.** Which of the Three Buckets does this move?\\r\\n- More customers\\r\\n- More value per customer\\r\\n- Less cost\\r\\n\\r\\nPlus a specific metric (response time, error rate, conversion rate, time-to-completion). **If the user can\'t name a bucket and a metric, skill stops.** *\\"If your automation doesn\'t move a number, why are you building it?\\"*\\r\\n\\r\\n**Output of Phase 2:** scoped automation spec written to `decisions/log.md` as a dated entry with all five answers + autonomy level + KPI. Durable record of what was decided and why.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Phase 3 — Machine handoff (build it)\\r\\n\\r\\nAsk: *\\"How do you want to ship this?\\"* Options ordered by Boring-is-Beautiful default:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Prompt-only** — saved prompt template the user runs by hand. Zero infrastructure. Highest manual involvement.\\r\\n2. **Deterministic skill** — SKILL.md that runs a script (no AI step). Best for transformations with clear rules.\\r\\n3. **AI-assisted skill** — SKILL.md with one AI call inside. Drafts, classifies, summarizes.\\r\\n4. **Sub-agent** — multi-step agent. Last resort. Only if the work genuinely needs reasoning + tool use.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Default selected = highest non-AI option that solves the problem.** User has to explicitly choose more autonomy.\\r\\n\\r\\nOnce chosen, route to the appropriate scaffolder:\\r\\n- `skill-creator` if available globally (Anthropic-shipped)\\r\\n- `skill-builder` if user has it locally\\r\\n- Otherwise write a SKILL.md / agent file inline with frontmatter, location, and contents\\r\\n\\r\\n**Every scaffolded artifact ships with these two headers at top:**\\r\\n\\r\\n```markdown\\r\\n---\\r\\nbike-method-phase: 1  # Phase 1 — Training wheels. Run manually first.\\r\\nthree-ms-attribution: |\\r\\n  Adapted from The Three Ms of AI™ © 2026 Nate Herk.\\r\\n---\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThis locks the user into Phase 1 of the Bike Method on first build. They can\'t silently skip manual validation. Phase advances only by explicit edit.\\r\\n\\r\\nSurface the Machine principles when scaffolding:\\r\\n- **Lego Principle** — smallest steps, zero-AI first if possible\\r\\n- **Validation Chain** — test each step before chaining\\r\\n- **Iteration Mindset** — ship the POC, expand from real usage\\r\\n\\r\\n## Output contract\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery `/level-up` run produces:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **One `decisions/log.md` entry** — dated, with the Method spec\\r\\n2. **One delivered improvement**: a prompt, skill, or agent file, or a verified repair of the selected existing workflow/routing\\r\\n3. **A one-screen close** — what was scoped, what was built, and the Bike Method Phase 1 reminder\\r\\n\\r\\n## Critical implementation rules\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **One interview = one artifact.** No multi-candidate parallel scoping.\\r\\n2. **Mindset phase always runs first.** Even if user comes in with a pre-formed idea.\\r\\n3. **EAD enforces \\"eliminate first.\\"** If the answer is Eliminate, exit cheerfully — that\'s a win, not a failure.\\r\\n4. **Default to the lowest autonomy level that works.** Push back on L4.\\r\\n5. **Boring-is-Beautiful default in Machine handoff.** Default = highest non-AI option.\\r\\n6. **Tie-to-KPI is mandatory.** If user can\'t name bucket + metric, skill stops.\\r\\n7. **Bike Method ships into every artifact.** `bike-method-phase: 1` in frontmatter.\\r\\n8. **Limit edits to `decisions/log.md` and the selected artifact.** An explicitly selected audit repair may update its existing workflow or routing files; preserve unrelated content. Other files remain read-only.\\r\\n9. **Trademark + attribution on output.** Every report and every scaffolded artifact references the framework.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Verification (for the implementer)\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Dry run on Nate\'s Herk-2** with no prompt. Expected: skill surfaces 2-3 candidates pulled from his recent activity, priorities, and top_pain. Generic output (\\"you should build a brief\\") = fail.\\r\\n- **Eliminate-first test.** Feed an obviously eliminate-able candidate. Expected: skill suggests Eliminate, exits, logs the win.\\r\\n- **L4 push-back test.** User asks for autonomous email-replier on first build. Expected: skill insists on L1/L2 first, won\'t ship L4 without explicit override.\\r\\n- **Boring-is-Beautiful test.** Candidate solvable with deterministic Python. Superwhisper is the app that does it, and the\\r\\n`dev/ai-os/superwhisper/` folder is its source of truth. Your job is to keep that folder right\\r\\nand get it into the app without him having to touch anything. He only ever presses Ctrl+Space.\\r\\n\\r\\nRead `dev/ai-os/superwhisper/AGENTS.md` first if this is a new session. This\\r\\nskill assumes those rules; it does not repeat them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The three requests\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1. A word or a correction (\\"Firecrow --> Firecrawl\\", \\"save Pre-workout\\")\\r\\n\\r\\nDecide which of two files it belongs in. This is where almost everything goes.\\r\\n- `vocabulary.md` is a hint list sent to the voice model. Keep it around 40 entries: names and\\r\\n  terms the model cannot know. On 2026-09-11 it was pushed to 654 (every replacement target\\r\\n  auto-added) and transcription got noticeably worse within the hour, so that rule is gone;\\r\\n  the sync sends exactly the listed terms. Add a vocabulary line only for a term the model\\r\\n  keeps getting wrong.\\r\\n\\r\\nA correction with an arrow is a replacement row only. \\"Save the word X\\" means a vocabulary\\r\\nline (if the model really cannot know it) plus replacement rows for how it gets mangled.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Think through the variants before writing.** One row per spelling he sends is not enough;\\r\\nhe sends the next mis-hearing ten minutes later. For each term, write rows for:\\r\\n\\r\\n- the exact form he sent, lowercase on the heard side\\r\\n- the same with a trailing period (`firecrow.`), because a one-word dictation gets\\r\\n  auto-punctuated and the rule will not match with the period attached\\r\\n- phonetic neighbours: swapped vowels (fisseha → faseya, fuseya, fasaya, fesaya), doubled\\r\\n  or dropped letters (firecrawll, firecraw), split or joined words (pre workout, preworkout,\\r\\n  cloudcode)\\r\\n- spoken forms of anything with punctuation: \\"at ... dot com\\", \\"dot study\\"\\r\\n- a casing pin when the wanted form has specific casing (`pre-workout` → `Pre-workout`,\\r\\n  `lsatprep.study` lowercase, `LSATU` → `LSAT U`)\\r\\n- the bare surname or bare product name, not only the full email or phrase\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not add a row whose heard side is an ordinary English word or number (\\"seven\\" → Steven,\\r\\n\\"white\\" → Whit, \\"care\\" → Charles, \\"and review\\" → blind review). It would fire inside normal\\r\\nsentences. When a scan suggests one of those, say so and leave it out.\\r\\n\\r\\nNote the trade-off on trailing-period rows: a sentence that genuinely ends with the word\\r\\nloses its full stop. Say this once when you add the first such row; do not repeat it.\\r\\n\\r\\nThen run the loop (below). A mode (\\"make a mode for ...\\")\\r\\n\\r\\nCopy the closest file in `modes/` to a new `modes/<key>.md`. Say the User Message is dictated speech.\\r\\n- Any mode whose output goes to an AI agent needs the \\"you are not an assistant\\" block with\\r\\n  WRONG/CORRECT pairs, or the model answers the dictation instead of cleaning it. Copy it\\r\\n  from `modes/Codex.md`.\\r\\n- Anything student-facing routes through `wiki/teaching-voice.md`: no em dashes, no hype\\r\\n  words, short lines, \\"Hi [Name],\\" / \\"Best, Joshua\\".\\r\\n- Turn on only the context the mode needs. Selection is captured at record start, clipboard\\r\\n  within 3 s before or during, application after transcription.\\r\\n- Language model: Joshua chose S1-Language (`sl-1`) for all modes on 2026-09-11 for speed.\\r\\n  Keep that unless he asks; `sw-Codex-4p5-sonnet` is the confirmed upgrade if a mode needs\\r\\n  judgment.\\r\\n\\r\\nThen run the loop. Add the mode to the table in `superwhisper/AGENTS.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 3. A scan (\\"what keeps going wrong\\", \\"scan my transcripts\\", or every week or so unprompted)\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/superwhisper/scan.py            # all history\\r\\npython C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/superwhisper/scan.py --since 7  # last week\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIt reads every recording\'s raw transcript and writes `research/SCAN-<date>.md` with four\\r\\nsections: near-misses of known terms (these become replacement rows), replacement rules\\r\\nthat did not fire after their date (means the app was not restarted, or the spelling\\r\\ndiffers), candidate terms seen often with varying spellings (worth adding), and the most\\r\\nused domain words.\\r\\n\\r\\nTurn the report into a short offer, not a dump: the rows you would add (and why), the ones\\r\\nyou are deliberately skipping (and why), and any mode-level improvement the transcripts\\r\\nsuggest (for example, if most of the week\'s dictations were instructions to an agent and\\r\\nthe Codex mode is not the active one, say so). Apply the safe rows in the same turn,\\r\\nrun the loop, and leave the judgment calls to him.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The loop\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery change ends the same way. `sync.py --restart` does all of it:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/superwhisper/sync.py --restart\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reads `vocabulary.md`, `replacements.md`, `modes/*.md`.\\r\\n2. Backs up the app\'s `settings.json`, then writes vocabulary, replacements, modeKeys, and\\r\\n   every mode file through the `\\\\\\\\localhost\\\\C$` path (the sandbox bypass).\\r\\n3. Quits Superwhisper and relaunches it through Task Scheduler so it runs outside the\\r\\n   sandbox, silently, in the background. Nothing appears on his screen; he keeps using\\r\\n   Ctrl+Space.\\r\\n4. Reads `modeKeys` back. The app rewrites that list at launch and drops any mode it\\r\\n   rejected, so this is the only proof that a change loaded. A write is not a load.\\r\\n\\r\\nReport the last line it prints (replacements / vocabulary / modes loaded). If the mode\\r\\ncount is lower than the number of files in `modes/`, a mode was rejected: diff the loaded\\r\\nlist against the files and fix before saying done.\\r\\n\\r\\n`python sync.py --check` shows the diff without writing, for when you want to confirm\\r\\nbefore touching anything.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Things not to do\\r\\n\\r\\n- Do not open the Settings window, the app, or anything visible after a restart. He asked\\r\\n  for this explicitly on 2026-09-11. If he needs Settings, `superwhisper://settings` or the\\r\\n  \\"Superwhisper Settings\\" shortcut on his Desktop opens it.\\r\\n- Do not launch `Superwhisper.exe` with Start-Process from this shell. It starts a\\r\\n  sandboxed second copy whose tray icon does not work. Only the scheduler route in\\r\\n  `sync.py`.\\r\\n- Do not edit the app\'s JSON by hand. Edit the vault files; the sync owns the JSON.\\r\\n- Do not pad the vocabulary. When in doubt, it is a replacement.\\r\\n- Do not batch his corrections for later. Each one lands, syncs, restarts, and is reported in\\r\\n  the turn it arrives, even mid-task.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Files\\r\\n\\r\\n| Path | Role |\\r\\n|---|---|\\r\\n| `dev/ai-os/superwhisper/AGENTS.md` | The rules. Read first. |\\r\\n| `dev/ai-os/superwhisper/vocabulary.md`, `replacements.md` | The lists. Edit these. |\\r\\n| `dev/ai-os/superwhisper/modes/*.md` | One file per mode. |\\r\\n| `dev/ai-os/superwhisper/sync.py` | Push + restart + verify. |\\r\\n| `dev/ai-os/superwhisper/scan.py` | Transcript scan → `research/SCAN-<date>.md`. |\\r\\n| `dev/ai-os/superwhisper/research/` | The 2026-09-11 customization report, sources, scans. |\\r\\n| `wiki/SUPERWHISPER-DICTIONARY.md` | Dated history ledger; append a line when something notable changes. |\\r\\n"}'}]

It is the one place for any operation on the LSAT U platform, and none of it uses Lovable.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Assign work on LSAT U\\r\\n\\r\\nAssign work, message students, and read how they are doing on LSAT U, all\\r\\nfrom the command line. No browser, no clicking. For complete interactive\\r\\nClassroom lessons, use the local `lsat-u-lessons` MCP or its direct Node\\r\\nfallback documented in the AI OS `lsat-u-platform-actions` skill. Both paths\\r\\npost through LSAT U\'s authenticated API and need no Lovable publish.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Authorization\\r\\n\\r\\nJoshua pre-authorized this on 2026-09-07: **a single named student is a go.**\\r\\nRun it, then report. Do not stop to ask permission first.\\r\\n\\r\\nConfirm before running when:\\r\\n\\r\\n- assigning to **3 or more students at once** — each one emails a real person\\r\\n- the student name is **ambiguous** (the script refuses and lists the matches)\\r\\n- the student is **Thaniuska Vivas** or **Amanda** — no platform account found\\r\\n- Joshua names someone absent from [[STUDENT-PLATFORM-IDENTITY-MAP]]\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is a deliberate, narrow exception to his global \\"draft, never send\\" rule.\\r\\nThat rule still holds for email, posts, and anything outside LSAT U.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The command\\r\\n\\r\\nEverything goes through one command: `system/scripts/lsatu` in the vault\\r\\n(`C:\\\\Users\\\\Joshu\\\\dev\\\\ai-os`). Run it with bash from the vault root.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Never** `cd projects/lsatu` and run `scripts/assign.ts` directly. That\\r\\ncheckout is on whatever branch another session left it on, sometimes with an\\r\\nuncommitted `assign.ts` that is missing flags. On 2026-09-23 it had no\\r\\n`--section`, `--due` or `--set`. The wrapper runs writes from\\r\\n`projects/.lsatu-ops`, a detached worktree it fast-forwards to `origin/main`\\r\\nbefore every run. It refuses to run if that copy has local edits.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Writes**\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign --student \\"Celia\\" --activity \\"Read, Recall, Colour\\"\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign --student \\"Lydia\\" --drill \\"main-conclusion-1\\"\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign --student \\"Dakota\\" --message \\"Start with PT105.S2 before Thursday.\\"\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign --student \\"Avneet\\" --section PT156.S2 --due 2026-09-26\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign --student \\"Avneet\\" --set \\"PT156.S2 (LR)\\"\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Many students at once.** The wrapper resolves every name first, and one bad\\r\\nname stops the batch before anyone is emailed. The 3+ confirmation rule above\\r\\nstill applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu assign-many \\"Celia, Lydia, Dakota\\" --drill \\"main-conclusion-1\\" --due 2026-09-26\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Reads.** These never write, so they are safe any time and need no confirmation:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu status \\"Celia\\"            # open work, overdue flags, last seen, recent sections\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu qtypes \\"Celia\\" --days 30  # accuracy by question type, weakest first\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu sections \\"Celia\\"          # recent timed sections with BR scores\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu overdue                   # every past-due unfinished item, all students\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu quiet --days 7            # students with open work, not seen in N days\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu students                  # every account, email, last seen\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu inbox --days 7            # messages students sent you, newest first\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu thread \\"Celia\\"            # the full message thread with one student\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Accounts, access, and Classroom upkeep** (`system/scripts/lsatu-admin.mjs`, same\\r\\nadmin login, calls the same `admin-manage-users` / `booking-pass-admin` edge\\r\\nfunctions the dashboard calls):\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu signups --days 30                  # who joined, and what access each has (NO ACCESS YET = waiting on you)\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu access \\"Venusa\\"                    # show every flag, on and off\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu access \\"Venusa\\" --template standard   # trial | standard | full, exactly the dashboard templates\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu access \\"Venusa\\" --grant drill,activity --revoke chat\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu archive \\"Name\\" --reason \\"finished\\"   # and: unarchive \\"Name\\"\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu items \\"Celia\\"                      # her open Classroom items WITH ids\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu due <item-id> 2026-09-30           # move a due date\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu unassign <item-id>                 # hide from her Classroom (archived; her work stays)\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu passes [\\"Celia\\"]                   # booking passes: used / total / owed\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu notifications                      # your unread admin notifications\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu read \\"Celia\\"                       # mark your thread with her read\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Review queues:**\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu drafts [--status draft|approved|posted|all]   # AI TA drafts waiting on you\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu draft <id>                          # full text\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu draft-set <id> approved|rejected|posted\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu draft-send <id>                     # message it to the student, then mark posted\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu uploads [--all]                     # student uploads not yet reviewed\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu upload-review <id> parsed|needs_review|failed\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu notes [--all]                       # session notes waiting on a match\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu note-resolve <ledger-id> \\"Celia\\"    # file the note under her\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu note-discard <ledger-id> [--reason \\"..\\"]\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu scan-notes                          # scan Drive for new session notes now\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu plans \\"Lydia\\"                       # her weekly plans and items\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Unsend a message:**\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu thread \\"Adriana\\" --ids          # message ids\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu unsend <message-id> [--dry-run]\\r\\nsystem/scripts/lsatu unsend-last \\"Adriana\\" [--dry-run]   # your most recent message to her\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThis removes only your own messages, never a student\'s. It reports whether\\r\\nshe has already opened the thread: if she has not, she never sees the\\r\\nmessage. A plain message makes no bell entry and no email, so removing it\\r\\nremoves every trace. An assignment\'s email cannot be recalled, and unsending\\r\\nits inbox message does not unassign the work; use `unassign` for that.\\r\\nDeleting is permanent, so confirm with Joshua every time unless he named the\\r\\nmessage in this turn.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Multi-line text is refused on purpose.** On Windows the npx shim cuts an\\r\\nargument at the first newline and drops everything after it, `--dry-run`\\r\\nincluded. On 2026-09-23 a \\"dry run\\" of `draft-send` really sent Adriana Varea\\r\\nthe first line of a draft. The wrapper now refuses any multi-line argument.\\r\\nMessages must be one line until `assign.ts` reads its text from a file.\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery write here takes `--dry-run`. Flag short names: practice, drill,\\r\\nclassroom, bootcamp, analytics, schedule, waj, journal, flagged, chat, export,\\r\\nta, activity. Templates always leave the \\"paying student\\" defaults on, the\\r\\nsame as the dashboard does.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Go without asking:** every read, `access` grants for one named student,\\r\\n`due`, and `read`. **Confirm first:** `archive`, `unarchive`, `unassign`,\\r\\n`--all-off`, and any `--revoke`, because each of these takes something away\\r\\nfrom a real student. **Not available here on purpose:** deleting a student\\r\\n(permanent), changing admin roles, and anything that edits app code or the\\r\\ndatabase schema. Those stay with Joshua in the dashboard or Lovable.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Other platform jobs that already have a home:** one-off booking links and\\r\\nnew passes go through the `booking-link` skill (`scripts/booking-link.ts`).\\r\\nAccommodations emails use the `accommodations-email` skill.\\r\\n\\r\\nAdd `--json` to any read when you want to compute on the output. `overdue` and\\r\\n`quiet` include former students, because the platform has no \\"former\\" flag.\\r\\nCross-check `students/roster.generated.md` before acting on either list.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen you are unsure what a student already has, run `status` before\\r\\nassigning. One call catches both double-assigns and the overdue pile.\\r\\n\\r\\nFlags: `--schedule YYYY-MM-DD` unlocks the work that morning. `--due YYYY-MM-DD`\\r\\nis due at the end of that local day and shows on the card and the calendar\\r\\nstrip. `--dry-run` resolves the student and the work and writes nothing — use it\\r\\nwhen the name is at all uncertain.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Dates are absolute.** \\"Due Saturday\\" means look up the date of the coming\\r\\nSaturday and pass that. On 2026-09-10 (a Thursday) Saturday was 2026-09-12; a\\r\\nhandoff once carried 09-13, which is the Sunday.\\r\\n\\r\\nTo pace a student over several days, run the command once per day with a\\r\\n`--schedule` on each. Each run is its own assignment, its own row, and its own\\r\\nemail, so she is told about each day rather than handed a block.\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery assignment lands on the home calendar strip and the cell opens that\\r\\nassignment — scheduled work on its unlock day, unscheduled work on the day you\\r\\nassigned it. Nothing needs to be written by hand to put work on the calendar;\\r\\nif an assignment is missing from the band, that is a bug to fix in\\r\\n`useClassroomHome`, not something to patch into `classroom_items`.\\r\\n\\r\\nAlways `--dry-run` first for a student you have not assigned to before in this\\r\\nsession. It costs one second and it is the only cheap way to catch a wrong\\r\\naccount.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Why a script and not a direct DB write\\r\\n\\r\\n`scripts/assign.ts` calls the app\'s **own** `assignWork()` from\\r\\n`src/lib/assignWork.ts`. Assigning touches seven tables — the assignment\\r\\nsnapshot, `classroom_items`, the conversation and its participants, `messages`,\\r\\n`notifications` — plus the email edge function, and it rolls the whole thing\\r\\nback if the classroom item or notify throws. There is no RPC and no edge\\r\\nfunction for it; it is client-side code.\\r\\n\\r\\nSo never hand-write these rows. A second implementation drifts from the UI the\\r\\nfirst time the app changes, and produces assignments subtly unlike the ones\\r\\nJoshua makes by clicking.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Credentials\\r\\n\\r\\nRead from `~/ai-os/.env`, which is **not** a git repo:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `LSATPREP_ADMIN_EMAIL`, `LSATPREP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` — already set\\r\\n\\r\\nNever put a credential in `projects/lsatu/.env`. That file **is tracked in git**\\r\\nand would be committed. The script signs in as Joshua and works under normal\\r\\nadmin RLS, the same permission path the UI uses.\\r\\n\\r\\n`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is deliberately **not** used even when present: it\\r\\nbypasses RLS on every write, so a script running as service_role would hide an\\r\\nRLS regression instead of hitting it. The script warns and falls back.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Expected output\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nAssign \\"Read, Recall, Colour\\" → Celia <celiacutler@gmail.com>\\r\\nAssigned. id=e83e2193-…\\r\\n  inbox ok · bell ok · email ok\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nA notify channel reading `FAILED` is **not** an assignment failure — the work is\\r\\nin her Classroom and only a message went missing. Report it, do not re-run.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Failure modes\\r\\n\\r\\n**`duplicate key … activity_assignments_active_unique`** — she already holds an\\r\\nactive assignment for this Activity. Not a bug; the DB refusing a double-assign.\\r\\nCheck what she has before re-trying (below).\\r\\n\\r\\n**`\\"X\\" is ambiguous`** — the script lists every matching account and stops.\\r\\nPick the full name or the email. Never guess: a misdirected assignment is\\r\\nsilent, because she simply never sees it.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Sign-in failed** — the credentials in `~/ai-os/.env` are wrong or the account\\r\\ngained MFA.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Checking what a student already has\\r\\n\\r\\n`system/scripts/lsatu status \\"Celia\\"` lists every open classroom item with its\\r\\ntype, status, assign date and due date, and flags anything overdue.\\r\\n\\r\\n## A PT section as timed homework\\r\\n\\r\\n`--section PT156.S2` (also accepts `PT156-S2`, `pt 156 s 2`) assigns one\\r\\nLogical Reasoning section to run under the real 35:00 section clock, with the\\r\\nofficial PrepTest header, exactly like a section inside a practice test.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhat the script does, verified end to end on 2026-09-10 on\\r\\n`joshua.fisseha01@gmail.com` (the test account):\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reads `public/data/PT156-S2-LR.json` and builds the qids\\r\\n   `PT156-S2-Q1 … Q25` in order. No file → it lists the sections that PT does\\r\\n   have and stops. Only LR sections are loaded; there is no RC/LG file set.\\r\\n2. Finds or creates the homework set titled **`PT156.S2 (LR)`** with exactly\\r\\n   those qids and `estimated_minutes = 35`. One set per section, reused; a\\r\\n   same-title set with different questions stops the run.\\r\\n3. Calls the app\'s own `assignWork({ kind: \'homework_set\' })`: assignment row,\\r\\n   classroom item (with `due_at`), inbox message, bell, email.\\r\\n4. Turns on `has_classroom_access` and `has_drill_access` if either was off,\\r\\n   because the set opens at `/classroom/:id` and runs at `/drill`.\\r\\n\\r\\nExpected output:\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nAssign \\"PT156.S2 (LR)\\" → josh <joshua.fisseha01@gmail.com>  (due 2026-09-13)\\r\\n  25 questions, timed 35:00 · set reused (ff0fe127-…)\\r\\nAssigned. id=04e154c8-…\\r\\n  inbox ok · bell ok · email ok\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Already assigned:** the script says\\r\\n`already has \\"PT156.S2 (LR)\\" (in_progress, assigned 2026-09-10)` and stops. A\\r\\nset can be re-issued only after that copy is `completed`. Do not work around\\r\\nit by making a second set.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Why the timer is real:** `src/lib/drillRunSpec.ts` `singleSectionOf()` sees\\r\\nthat every qid is one PT+section and runs it as `full-section` (35-minute\\r\\ncountdown) instead of `type-drill` (a stopwatch). Shipped with `--section` in\\r\\nPR #113, merged 2026-09-11.\\r\\n\\r\\n`--set \\"<title or id>\\"` assigns any existing homework set, timed or not, with\\r\\nthe same guards.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Read, Recall, Colour specifically\\r\\n\\r\\nAssign the title **\\"Read, Recall, Colour\\"** — the section-library door. She then\\r\\npicks any of 12 seeded sections (PT1.S3, PT21.S3, PT101.S2, PT102.S3, PT103.S1,\\r\\nPT104.S1, PT105.S1, PT105.S2, PT106.S2, PT112.S4, PT134.S3, PT140.S1), 25 min\\r\\neach. Every attempt is kept; re-running saves a new attempt.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe script prefers the exact title, so it resolves to the door rather than one\\r\\nof the 12 sections. Pass a `read-recall-colour-pt*-s*` slug only to pin her to\\r\\none section deliberately.\\r\\n\\r\\n## One headless backend, never Lovable for content\\r\\n\\r\\nDecided by Joshua on 2026-09-23 and refined 2026-09-29. `system/scripts/lsatu`\\r\\nis the headless path for work assignments, messaging, and student data. The\\r\\nlocal `lsat-u-lessons` MCP wraps `system/scripts/lsatu-admin.mjs post-lesson`\\r\\nfor interactive lesson assignment and exact HTML verification. It is a local\\r\\nwrapper over the same authenticated backend, not a hosted connector or an app\\r\\ndeploy. Lovable is only for changing the app\'s own code.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The hosted connector (MCP): exists, not used\\r\\n\\r\\nLSAT U also runs a real MCP server, `lsat-u-mcp` v0.3.0, at\\r\\n`https://atrcqxpmqrynmtvvyjju.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp`. Verified live on\\r\\n2026-09-23: it returns 401 without a token and serves OAuth discovery. The\\r\\nsource is `src/lib/mcp/` in the app repo, deployed as the `mcp` edge function.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Connect:** claude.ai → Settings → Connectors → add a custom connector with\\r\\n  that URL, then sign in with an LSAT U account. There is no key to paste.\\r\\n- **Who gets the admin tools:** any account with the `admin` role in\\r\\n  `user_roles`. To grant someone access, give their account that role; remove\\r\\n  the role to revoke it. Students who connect see only their own data.\\r\\n- **Tools today:** `find_students`, `list_students`, `list_homework_sets`,\\r\\n  `assign_homework`, `assign_passage_map_homework`, `post_classroom_note`,\\r\\n  `send_note`, `get_assignment_status`, plus the student-side `get_my_profile`,\\r\\n  `list_my_homework` and `list_my_classroom_items`.\\r\\n- **In the CLI but not the connector:** activities, guided drills, bootcamps,\\r\\n  timed `--section` with due dates, and every analytics read. Adding them\\r\\n  means app code plus a Lovable deploy, which needs Joshua\'s credit\\r\\n  confirmation first.\\r\\n\\r\\nOn this laptop, use the CLI: it does more and costs nothing. The connector is\\r\\nfor when Joshua is away from the laptop, or when someone else needs access.\\r\\n\\r\\nRunning `vite-node` inside the app repo rewrites\\r\\n`supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts` with a local path (the `@lovable.dev/mcp-js`\\r\\nVite plugin). Never commit that change. The wrapper restores the file after\\r\\neach run.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Related\\r\\n\\r\\nVault: `wiki/ASSIGN-AN-ACTIVITY.md` (the browser path and what fires),\\r\\n`wiki/STUDENT-PLATFORM-IDENTITY-MAP.md` (which account is which student —\\r\\n33 platform accounts, 20 real students, 13 unmatched).\\r\\n"}'}]
