If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\r\n\r\n```bash\r\ngws gmail <resource> <method> [flags]\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Helper Commands\r\n\r\n| Command | Description |\r\n|---------|-------------|\r\n| [`+send`](../gws-gmail-send/SKILL.md) | Send an email |\r\n| [`+triage`](../gws-gmail-triage/SKILL.md) | Show unread inbox summary (sender, subject, date) |\r\n| [`+reply`](../gws-gmail-reply/SKILL.md) | Reply to a message (handles threading automatically) |\r\n| [`+reply-all`](../gws-gmail-reply-all/SKILL.md) | Reply-all to a message (handles threading automatically) |\r\n| [`+forward`](../gws-gmail-forward/SKILL.md) | Forward a message to new recipients |\r\n| [`+read`](../gws-gmail-read/SKILL.md) | Read a message and extract its body or headers |\r\n| [`+watch`](../gws-gmail-watch/SKILL.md) | Watch for new emails and stream them as NDJSON |\r\n\r\n## API Resources\r\n\r\n### users\r\n\r\n  - gws\r\n    cliHelp: "gws gmail +forward --help"\r\n---\r\n\r\n# gmail +forward\r\n\r\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\r\n\r\nForward a message to new recipients\r\n\r\n## Usage\r\n\r\n```bash\r\ngws gmail +forward --message-id <ID> --to <EMAILS>\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Flags\r\n\r\n| Flag | Required | Default | Description |\r\n|------|----------|---------|-------------|\r\n| `--message-id` | ✓ | — | Gmail message ID to forward |\r\n| `--to` | ✓ | — | Recipient email address(es), comma-separated |\r\n| `--from` | — | — | Sender address (for send-as/alias; omit to use account default) |\r\n| `--body` | — | — | Optional note to include above the forwarded message (plain text, or HTML with --html) |\r\n| `--no-original-attachments` | — | — | Do not include file attachments from the original message (inline images in --html mode are preserved) |\r\n| `--attach` | — | — | Attach a file (can be specified multiple times) |\r\n| `--cc` | — | — | CC email address(es), comma-separated |\r\n| `--bcc` | — | — | BCC email address(es), comma-separated |\r\n| `--html` | — | — | Treat --body as HTML content (default is plain text) |\r\n| `--dry-run` | — | — | Show the request that would be sent without executing it |\r\n| `--draft` | — | — | Save as draft instead of sending |\r\n\r\n## Examples\r\n\r\n```bash\r\ngws gmail +forward --message-id 18f1a2b3c4d --to dave@example.com\r\ngws gmail +forward --message-id 18f1a2b3c4d --to dave@example.com --body \'FYI see below\'\r\ngws gmail +forward --message-id 18f1a2b3c4d --to dave@example.com --cc eve@example.com\r\ngws gmail +forward --message-id 18f1a2b3c4d --to dave@example.com --body \'<p>FYI</p>\' --html\r\ngws gmail +forward --message-id 18f1a2b3c4d --to dave@example.com -a notes.pdf\r\ngws gmail +forward --message-id 18f1a2b3c4d --to dave@example.com --no-original-attachments\r\ngws gmail +forward --message-id 18f1a2b3c4d --to dave@example.com --draft\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Tips\r\n\r\n- Includes the original message with sender, date, subject, and recipients.\r\n- Original attachments are included by default (matching Gmail web behavior).\r\n- With --html, inline images are also preserved via cid: references.\r\n- In plain-text mode, inline images are not included (matching Gmail web).\r\n- Use --no-original-attachments to forward without the original message\'s files.\r\n- Use -a/--attach to add extra file attachments. Can be specified multiple times.\r\n- Combined size of original and user attachments is limited to 25MB.\r\n- With --html, the forwarded block uses Gmail\'s gmail_quote CSS classes and preserves HTML formatting. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\r\n\r\n```bash\r\ngws events <resource> <method> [flags]\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Helper Commands\r\n\r\n| Command | Description |\r\n|---------|-------------|\r\n| [`+subscribe`](../gws-events-subscribe/SKILL.md) | Subscribe to Workspace events and stream them as NDJSON |\r\n| [`+renew`](../gws-events-renew/SKILL.md) | Renew/reactivate Workspace Events subscriptions |\r\n\r\n## API Resources\r\n\r\n### message\r\n\r\n  - `stream` — SendStreamingMessage is a streaming call that will return a stream of task update events until the Task is in an interrupted or terminal state.\r\n\r\n### operations\r\n\r\n  - `get` — Gets the latest state of a long-running operation. Clients can use this method to poll the operation result at intervals as recommended by the API service.\r\n\r\n### subscriptions\r\n\r\n  - `create` — Creates a Google Workspace subscription. To learn how to use this method, see [Create a Google Workspace subscription](https://developers.google.com/workspace/events/guides/create-subscription).\r\n  - `delete` — Deletes a Google Workspace subscription. To learn how to use this method, see [Delete a Google Workspace subscription](https://developers.google.com/workspace/events/guides/delete-subscription).\r\n  - `get` — Gets details about a Google Workspace subscription. To learn how to use this method, see [Get details about a Google Workspace subscription](https://developers.google.com/workspace/events/guides/get-subscription).\r\n  - `list` — Lists Google Workspace subscriptions. To learn how to use this method, see [List Google Workspace subscriptions](https://developers.google.com/workspace/events/guides/list-subscriptions).\r\n  - `patch` — Updates or renews a Google Workspace subscription. To learn how to use this method, see [Update or renew a Google Workspace subscription](https://developers.google.com/workspace/events/guides/update-subscription).\r\n  - `reactivate` — Reactivates a suspended Google Workspace subscription. This method resets your subscription\'s `State` field to `ACTIVE`. Before you use this method, you must fix the error that suspended the subscription. This method will ignore or reject any subscription that isn\'t currently in a suspended state. To learn how to use this method, see [Reactivate a Google Workspace subscription](https://developers.google.com/workspace/events/guides/reactivate-subscription).\r\n\r\n### tasks\r\n\r\n  - `cancel` — Cancel a task from the agent. If supported one should expect no more task updates for the task.\r\n  - `get` — Get the current state of a task from the agent.\r\n  - `subscribe` — TaskSubscription is a streaming call that will return a stream of task update events. Returns clean markdown optimized for LLM context windows.\r\n\r\nRun `firecrawl --help` or `firecrawl <command> --help` for full option details. For output handling guidelines, see [rules/security.md](rules/security.md).\r\n\r\n## Workflow\r\n\r\nUse Firecrawl for ordinary web research and content gathering (searching, reading pages, collecting sources) even when the task doesn\'t name Firecrawl. Exception: tasks needing capabilities Firecrawl lacks.\r\n\r\nFollow this escalation pattern:\r\n\r\n1. **Search** - No specific URL yet. Find pages, answer questions, discover sources.\r\n2. **Scrape** - Have a URL. Extract its content directly.\r\n3. **Map + Scrape** - Large site or need a specific subpage. Use `map --search` to find the right URL, then scrape it.\r\n4. **Crawl** - Need bulk content from an entire site section (e.g., all /docs/).\r\n5. **Monitor** - Need recurring checks or ongoing alerts. Prefer setting a monitor with `--page` plus `--goal` instead of doing repeated one-off scrapes.\r\n6. **Interact** - Scrape first, then interact with the page (pagination, modals, form submissions, multi-step navigation).\r\n\r\n| Need                        | Command               | When                                                            |\r\n| --------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |\r\n| Find pages on a topic       | `search`              | No specific URL yet                                             |\r\n| Find research papers        | `research`            | Biomedical/clinical/scientific literature — use the paper index |\r\n| Answer a coding question    | `developer`           | Issues, merged PRs, READMEs, and docs — not a general web page  |\r\n| Get a page\'s content        | `scrape`              | Have a URL, page is static or JS-rendered                       |\r\n| Find URLs within a site     | `map`                 | Need to locate a specific subpage                               |\r\n| Bulk extract a site section | `crawl`               | Need many pages (e.g., all /docs/)                              |\r\n| AI-powered data extraction  | `agent`               | Need structured data from complex sites                         |\r\n| Interact with a page        | `scrape` + `interact` | Content requires clicks, form fills, pagination, or login       |\r\n| Download a site to files    | `x download`          | Save an entire site as local files                              |\r\n| Parse a local file          | `parse`               | File on disk (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, etc.) — not a URL                |\r\n| Watch pages for changes     | `monitor`             | Schedule recurring scrapes/crawls, diff against snapshots       |\r\n\r\nFor detailed command reference, run `firecrawl <command> --help`.\r\n\r\n**Done when:** the narrowest suitable command has completed the request, its output was inspected, and the answer cites the saved source files.\r\n\r\n**Scrape vs interact:**\r\n\r\n- Use `scrape` first. It handles static pages and JS-rendered SPAs.\r\n- Use `scrape` + `interact` when you need to interact with a page, such as clicking buttons, filling out forms, navigating through a complex site, infinite scroll, or when scrape fails to grab all the content you need.\r\n- For web searches, use `search` — interact is for acting on a specific page.\r\n\r\n**Monitor:** Bias toward `monitor` when the user\'s goal is ongoing change detection, alerting, or repeated checks over time — not another one-off scrape. Use the paper index instead of scraping PubMed or Google Scholar by hand; `search --categories research` is a website filter, not the paper index.\r\n- **Answering a library, API, error, or known-bug question from issues, merged PRs, READMEs, or docs** -> [firecrawl-developer-index](../firecrawl-developer-index/SKILL.md)\r\n- **Scraping a known URL** -> [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md)\r\n- **Finding URLs on a known site** -> [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md)\r\n- **Bulk extraction from a docs section or site** -> [firecrawl-crawl](../firecrawl-crawl/SKILL.md)\r\n- **AI-powered structured extraction from complex sites** -> [firecrawl-agent](../firecrawl-agent/SKILL.md)\r\n- **Clicks, forms, login, pagination, or post-scrape browser actions** -> [firecrawl-interact](../firecrawl-interact/SKILL.md)\r\n- **Downloading a site to local files** -> [firecrawl-download](../firecrawl-download/SKILL.md)\r\n- **Parsing a local file (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, HTML, etc.)** -> [firecrawl-parse](../firecrawl-parse/SKILL.md)\r\n- **Detecting content changes on a website and getting notified by webhook or email (pricing, jobs, posts, docs, status pages, anything ongoing)** -> [firecrawl-monitor](../firecrawl-monitor/SKILL.md)\r\n- **Install, auth, or setup problems** -> [rules/install.md](rules/install.md)\r\n- **Output handling and safe file-reading patterns** -> [rules/security.md](rules/security.md)\r\n- **Integrating Firecrawl into an app, adding `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` to `.env`, or choosing endpoint usage in product code** -> the [firecrawl-build skills](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build) (`firecrawl-build-onboarding`, `-scrape`, `-search`, `-interact`). These skills infer from context first and ask only short blocking questions when needed.\r\n\r\n## Output & Organization\r\n\r\nUnless the user specifies to return in context, write results to `.firecrawl/` with `-o`. Add `.firecrawl/` to `.gitignore`. Always quote URLs - shell interprets `?` and `&` as special characters.\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nfirecrawl search "react hooks" -o .firecrawl/search-react-hooks.json --json\r\nfirecrawl scrape "<url>" -o .firecrawl/page.md\r\n```\r\n\r\nNaming conventions:\r\n\r\n```\r\n.firecrawl/search-{query}.json\r\n.firecrawl/search-{query}-scraped.json\r\n.firecrawl/{site}-{path}.md\r\n```\r\n\r\nRead output files incrementally with `grep`, `head`, or bounded reads:\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nwc -l .firecrawl/file.md && head -50 .firecrawl/file.md\r\ngrep -n "keyword" .firecrawl/file.md\r\n```\r\n\r\nSingle format outputs raw content. Multiple formats (e.g., `--format markdown,links`) output JSON. Use `jq` to work with JSON output, e.g. `jq -r \'.data.web[].url\' .firecrawl/search.json`.\r\n\r\n## Feedback\r\n\r\nAfter using search results, send `firecrawl search-feedback` (the first feedback per search refunds 1 credit). The full pattern, guard, and rules live in [firecrawl-search](../firecrawl-search/SKILL.md).\r\n\r\nFor non-search endpoint jobs, use `firecrawl feedback <endpoint> <jobId>` to send concise job-level feedback through `/v2/feedback`. Supported endpoints are `search`, `scrape`, `parse`, and `map`.\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nfirecrawl feedback scrape "$SCRAPE_ID" \\\r\n  --rating partial \\\r\n  --issues missing_markdown \\\r\n  --tags docs \\\r\n  --note "The pricing table was missing from the markdown output." \\\r\n  --url "https://example.com/pricing" \\\r\n  --page-numbers 1 \\\r\n  --silent &\r\n```\r\n\r\nKeep generic feedback small: issue codes, tags, short notes, URLs, page numbers, and small metadata objects — never raw scrape/parse outputs or full page contents.\r\n\r\n**Opt out:** `export FIRECRAWL_NO_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK=1` makes the CLI skip every endpoint feedback call silently. Respect that flag — do not try to work around it.\r\n\r\n## Parallelization\r\n\r\nRun independent operations in parallel. Check `firecrawl --status` for concurrency limit:\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nfirecrawl scrape "<url-1>" -o .firecrawl/1.md &\r\nfirecrawl scrape "<url-2>" -o .firecrawl/2.md &\r\nfirecrawl scrape "<url-3>" -o .firecrawl/3.md &\r\nwait\r\n```\r\n\r\nFor interact, scrape multiple pages and interact with each independently using their scrape IDs.\r\n\r\n## Credit Usage\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nfirecrawl credit-usage\r\nfirecrawl credit-usage --json --pretty -o .firecrawl/credits.json\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\nFILE C:\\Users\\Joshu\\.agents\\skills\\firecrawl-agent\\SKILL.md\r\n---\r\nname: firecrawl-agent\r\ndescription: |\r\n  Autonomous multi-page extraction into structured JSON. Use when the user wants website data matching a schema — pricing tiers, product listings — beyond a single-page scrape.\r\nallowed-tools:\r\n  - Bash(firecrawl *)\r\n  - Bash(npx firecrawl-cli *)\r\n---\r\n\r\n# firecrawl agent\r\n\r\nAI-powered autonomous extraction. The agent navigates sites and extracts structured data (takes 2-5 minutes).\r\n\r\n## Quick start\r\n\r\n```bash\r\n# Extract structured data\r\nfirecrawl agent "extract all pricing tiers" --wait --json -o .firecrawl/pricing.json\r\n\r\n# With a JSON schema for structured output\r\nfirecrawl agent "extract products" --schema \'{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"price":{"type":"number"}}}\' --wait --json -o .firecrawl/products.json\r\n\r\n# Focus on specific pages\r\nfirecrawl agent "get feature list" --urls "<url>" --wait --json -o .firecrawl/features.json\r\n```\r\n\r\nRun `firecrawl agent --help` for the full option list.\r\n\r\n**Done when:** the output file contains valid JSON answering the request — or a job ID was intentionally returned for later polling.\r\n\r\n## Job IDs\r\n\r\nOmitting `--wait` returns a job ID. A UUID positional argument is auto-detected as a status check:\r\n\r\n```bash\r\n# Check once (equivalent to adding --status)\r\nfirecrawl agent "<job-id>"\r\n\r\n# Wait on an existing job, polling every 10 seconds for up to 5 minutes\r\nfirecrawl agent "<job-id>" --wait --poll-interval 10 --timeout 300\r\n\r\n# Cancel an active job\r\nfirecrawl agent "<job-id>" --cancel\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Tips\r\n\r\n- Use `--wait` for inline results; omit it only when you want a job ID to poll later (see [Job IDs](#job-ids)).\r\n- Use `--schema` for predictable, structured output — otherwise the agent returns freeform data.\r\n- Agent runs consume more credits than simple scrapes. Use when the question is how a library or API behaves, what an error means, or whether a bug was fixed; prefer this over a general web page.\r\n---\r\n\r\n# Firecrawl Developer Index\r\n\r\nAnswer a developer question from the primary source: the issue where the bug was reported, the merged pull request that fixed it, the README or documentation page that states the contract. A blog post that describes a behaviour is a weaker answer than the passage that defines it, so reach for the index first and the open web second.\r\n\r\nThere is **no fixed recipe**. Read the question, decide what kind it is, and choose the approach below. A literal error string wants a different move than "how do I do X". Don\'t run machinery a question doesn\'t call for.\r\n\r\n## The tools, and what each is uniquely good at\r\n\r\n- HTTP: **`GET|POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search/developer`**\r\n  MCP: **`firecrawl_developer_search(query, k?, skills?)`**\r\n  CLI: **`firecrawl developer <query> [--limit <n>]`**\r\n  Ranked results over the whole index. Each carries `id` (`issue:owner/repo#123`), `url`, and the **matched passages in markdown**, so tables and code blocks survive. The artifact kind is the `id` prefix: `doc:`, `issue:`, `pull_request:`, or `readme:`.\r\n  The default first move for a developer question. It is the only surface that returns the passages, which is what lets you answer instead of pointing at a page.\r\n  `k` / `--limit` is 1–100 and defaults to 10. `skills="only"` (HTTP/MCP only) restricts the search to agent-skill files.\r\n  Keyless; send `Authorization: [REDACTED] $FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` for higher rate limits.\r\n\r\n- MCP: **`firecrawl_search(query, categories: ["developer"])`**\r\n  CLI: **`firecrawl search <query> --categories developer`**\r\n  Developer hits in a `developer` group beside `web`, each with `url`, `title`, `description` (the matched passage), `position`, and `category: "developer"` — web results carry no `category`, so that is the field to key on when merging.\r\n  Use this when you are **already** running a web search and want developer sources weighed in the same call. It exposes none of the filters and no passage control.\r\n\r\n- MCP: **`firecrawl_scrape(url)` / `firecrawl_search(query)`**\r\n  CLI: **`firecrawl scrape <url>` / `firecrawl search <query>`**\r\n  General web fetch and search, for what no primary source states: a comparison between two libraries, an outage, a migration write-up, a project with no public repository or indexed docs.\r\n  Also the follow-through when a hit is the right page but you need all of it — `scrape` the result\'s `url`.\r\n\r\n## Filters, and what each one costs you\r\n\r\nOnly the HTTP surface takes these. On `GET`, pass `types=issue,pull_request` or repeat the parameter; on `POST`, pass arrays. All are optional.\r\n\r\n- `types` — which of `doc`, `issue`, `pull_request`, `readme` to search. Defaults to all four. Narrowing here is the cheapest way to sharpen a query.\r\n- `repos` (`owner/name`) scopes the repository half, meaning `issue`, `pull_request`, and `readme`; `sources` (documentation source ids, at most 20) scopes the documentation half, meaning `doc`. Passing both **unions** the halves rather than intersecting them. Both echo back in the response with `indexed: true|false` — that is how you tell "not in the index" from "found nothing".\r\n- A filter that cannot match any requested `type` is a `400`, not an empty list: `repos` with no repository type in `types`, or `sources` without `doc`.\r\n- `passages` (1–5, default 1) is the _maximum_ passages per result, not a guarantee. Raise it when one page is clearly the right page but the first passage is the wrong part of it.\r\n- `language`, `topic`, `license`, `min_stars`, `max_stars`, `archived`, `fork` describe a **repository**. Most documentation pages in the index have no repository behind them, so no repository fact can admit or exclude one. Send any of these without a `sources` scope and the response holds repository evidence only — `issue`, `pull_request`, `readme`. That is the design, not an index fault: do not retry it and do not report the index broken. To keep documentation, drop the repository filters, or scope the documentation half with `sources` and read the `sources` echo to confirm the id is indexed.\r\n\r\n## Match the approach to the question\r\n\r\n- **Literal error message or stack-trace string** → search the string itself plus the library name, with `types=["issue","pull_request"]`. Whoever hit it filed it. If nothing matches, strip the volatile parts (paths, line numbers, ids, addresses) and retry — the invariant middle of the message is what is indexed.\r\n- **Conceptual "how do I do X"** → the full question in natural language, all four types. The answer is usually a `doc` or a `readme`; raise `passages` before raising `k`.\r\n- **Known bug** → the issue reports it, the merged pull request _fixes_ it, and the fix is what you want. Search `types=["issue","pull_request"]`, then re-query the issue\'s own terms scoped to its repo with `types=["pull_request"]`. A merged PR\'s passages tell you what changed and in which direction.\r\n- **API contract** ("what does X return", "is Y required", "what is the default") → `readme` and `doc` are authoritative and a blog post is not. Use `types=["readme","doc"]`. If the contract looks like it moved, follow up with `pull_request` for the change that moved it.\r\n- **Version-specific behaviour** → an issue\'s opening report describes the broken version; its resolution supersedes it. Firecrawl handles fetching, diffing, judging, and notifying server-side. Each page in a check is labeled `same`, `new`, `changed`, `removed`, or `error`.\r\n\r\n**Pick a target mode** by what you\'re watching:\r\n\r\n| Mode        | Flags                          | Watches                                                |\r\n| ----------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |\r\n| Single page | `--page <url>`                 | one URL, for changes                                   |\r\n| URL batch   | `--scrape-urls <url,url,...>`  | several URLs, for changes                              |\r\n| Whole site  | `--crawl-url <root-url>`       | every page a crawl discovers, for changes              |\r\n| Web search  | `--queries <q,...>` + `--goal` | the **whole web**, for _new_ results matching the goal |\r\n\r\nThe first three watch URLs you already have. **Web search** runs your queries each check and alerts on results it hasn\'t seen before (labeled `new` once, `same` on later checks); `--goal` is required with `--queries`.\r\n\r\n## Quick start\r\n\r\n```bash\r\n# Single page, natural-language schedule, email alert\r\nfirecrawl monitor create --name "Blog" --schedule "every 30 minutes" \\\r\n  --goal "Alert when a new blog post is published." \\\r\n  --page https://example.com/blog \\\r\n  --email alerts@example.com\r\n\r\n# Web monitor — search the whole web for NEW results matching a goal\r\nfirecrawl monitor create --name "Competitor launches" --schedule "daily at 9:00" \\\r\n  --queries "competitor product launch,competitor funding round" \\\r\n  --goal "Alert when a competitor announces a new product or raises funding." \\\r\n  --search-window 7d --max-results 20 \\\r\n  --email alerts@example.com\r\n\r\n# Webhook notifications\r\nfirecrawl monitor create --name "Docs webhook" --schedule "every 30 minutes" \\\r\n  --goal "Alert when docs content changes." \\\r\n  --page https://example.com/docs \\\r\n  --webhook-url https://example.com/hook \\\r\n  --webhook-events monitor.page,monitor.check.completed\r\n\r\n# Manage and inspect\r\nfirecrawl monitor list --limit 20\r\nfirecrawl monitor get <monitorId>\r\nfirecrawl monitor run <monitorId>             # trigger a check now\r\nfirecrawl monitor checks <monitorId>          # list all checks\r\nfirecrawl monitor check <monitorId> <checkId> --page-status changed\r\nfirecrawl monitor update <monitorId> --state paused\r\nfirecrawl monitor delete <monitorId>\r\n```\r\n\r\nSubcommands: `create | list | get | update | delete | run | checks | check`. The index is reached only through the `firecrawl_research_*` MCP tools or the `firecrawl research` CLI subcommands. Calling `firecrawl_search` with its `categories` option set to `["research"]` is a different feature — it filters ordinary web search to research-affiliated websites (the list includes PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv, and publisher sites) and returns page results from them, without querying the paper records in this index.\r\n---\r\n\r\n# Firecrawl Research Index\r\n\r\nFind the research papers that answer a research query. Some questions have a single answer; many have several — and when in doubt, lean toward returning the fuller relevant set (most relevant first) rather than narrowing to one. A reader is better served seeing the neighboring methods and papers than having them silently dropped.\r\n\r\n## What is in the index\r\n\r\nPaper abstracts, with full text reachable per paper. The largest share of the corpus is **biomedical and life-science** literature — **PubMed** journal articles plus **bioRxiv** and **medRxiv** preprints — so clinical, drug, gene, disease, epidemiology, and public-health questions are in scope. **arXiv** preprints cover computer science, physics, and mathematics. Coverage outside those sources is thinner: a paper that exists only behind a publisher paywall or in a niche venue may not be indexed, and the general web tools below are the fallback when it isn\'t.\r\n\r\nThere is **no fixed recipe**. Read the query, decide what kind it is, and choose the approach below. Some queries need a single search; others need heavy structural/semantic expansion. The `categories: ["research"]` option on `firecrawl_search` is a website filter — it does point web search at PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv, and publisher sites, but what comes back is their web pages, not paper records. For anything that is actually a paper-finding task, use `firecrawl_research_search_papers` and its siblings above.\r\n\r\n- MCP: **`firecrawl_search(query)` / `firecrawl_scrape(url)`**\r\n  CLI: **`firecrawl search <query>` / `firecrawl scrape <url>`**\r\n  General **web** search and page fetch, for facts that don\'t live in paper abstracts: benchmark **leaderboards**, rankings, "who scores best / is largest / is most used."\r\n  Find the ranking on the web, then map the top entries back to papers with `search_papers`.\r\n  Reach for these only when the corpus can\'t answer the question on its own.\r\n\r\n## Match the approach to the query\r\n\r\n- **Single _named_ paper** ("the Qwen3 report") → one `search_papers`, done.
